definition_zh: 中立的；中性的；不带电的；空挡的；中性色的
definition_en: not taking either side in a conflict, neither acid nor alkaline, carrying no charge, or being neither one nor the other of two
core_image: 拔河绳上的红布停在两条界线正中间：两边都不到
scene: 裁判站在两名摔跤手中间，双臂下垂，不偏向任何一方。 A referee stands between two wrestlers with both arms down and stays neutral, favouring neither.
sceneCN: 这里 neutral 是「不选边、不介入」（第 2 个义项：在两方冲突中不偏向任何一方）；句意：裁判站在两名摔跤手之间，双臂下垂，保持中立，不偏向任何一方。图中可辨识物件：摔跤垫、两名选手、居中站立的裁判、下垂的双臂；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 中立的；中性的；不带电的；空挡的
中立者；中立国；（机械）空挡

senses.title: Alchemical balance: opposing elements in proportion
senses.titleCN: 炼金术的平衡：对立元素按比例相抵
senses.definition: in alchemy, of a substance made from opposing elements that balance each other exactly
senses.definitionCN: 在炼金术中，指由相互对立的元素按比例恰好相抵而成的物质
senses.example: Alchemists called a body neutral when fire and water balanced in it.
senses.exampleCN: 当火与水在物体中相抵平衡时，炼金术士称该物体为 neutral。
senses.why: Neutral is first recorded in the 1540s in alchemy, where opposite qualities were thought to cancel each other. The core picture is a scale that stops exactly in the middle.
senses.whyCN: neutral 最早记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，用于炼金术，当时认为对立的性质会相互抵消。核心画面是一架恰好停在正中的天平。

senses.title: Not taking sides: outside a conflict
senses.definition: not supporting either party in a dispute, war, or argument
senses.definitionCN: 在争端、战争或争论中不支持任何一方
senses.example: The referee stayed neutral and let both sides speak.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判保持中立，让双方都把话说完了。
senses.why: The alchemical balance became a social one: two opposing sides cancel, and the person in the middle belongs to neither. This sense is recorded alongside the first.
senses.whyCN: 炼金术的平衡变成了社会的平衡：两个对立面相互抵消，中间的人不属于任何一边。这个义项与最早义项同时被记录。

senses.title: Chemistry: neither acid nor alkaline
senses.definition: of a solution, having a pH near seven, neither acidic nor basic
senses.definitionCN: 指溶液 pH 接近七，既非酸性也非碱性
senses.example: Pure water is neutral, with a pH close to seven.
senses.exampleCN: 纯水是中性的，pH 接近七。
senses.why: Chemistry took the balance image literally: acid and alkali cancel, and the middle point is neutral. The sense is recorded from the 1660s.
senses.whyCN: 化学把这个平衡意象落到实处：酸与碱相抵，中间点就是中性。该义项记录于 17 世纪 60 年代。

senses.title: Not a belligerent: outside the war
senses.titleCN: 非交战国：站在战争之外
senses.definition: of a country or ship, not belonging to either side in a war
senses.definitionCN: 指国家或船只不属于战争中的任何一方
senses.example: Neutral shipping was allowed through the blockade.
senses.exampleCN: 中立国的船只被允许通过封锁线。
senses.why: A state can hold the same position as the referee: it takes no side, so its ships and ports stay outside the fighting. The sense is recorded from 1711.
senses.whyCN: 国家可以处在和裁判相同的位置：不选边，因此它的船只与港口留在战斗之外。该义项记录于 1711 年。

senses.title: Colour: low saturation, easy to live with
senses.definition: of a colour, muted and close to grey or beige, used as a quiet base
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色柔和、接近灰或米色，用作安静的底色
senses.example: The room was painted in neutral greys and warm beiges.
senses.exampleCN: 房间刷成了中性灰和暖米色。
senses.why: A muted colour sits between the strong hues and commits to none. The balance image moves from substances to light, and the sense is recorded from 1821.
senses.whyCN: 柔和的颜色处在各种强烈色相之间，不偏向任何一种。平衡意象从物质移到光线，该义项记录于 1821 年。

senses.title: Electrical neutrality: no net charge
senses.definition: having equal positive and negative charge, so that no net charge remains
senses.definitionCN: 正负电荷相等，因此没有净电荷残留
senses.example: A neutron carries no charge and is electrically neutral.
senses.exampleCN: 中子不带电荷，是电中性的。
senses.why: Positive and negative charges cancel exactly as acid and alkali cancel. The word's balance is now counted in charge rather than in qualities.
senses.whyCN: 正负电荷的相抵，正如酸与碱的相抵。这个词的平衡现在以电荷计算，而不是以性质计算。

senses.title: A neutral party: the person or state in the middle
senses.titleCN: 中立的一方：处在中间的人或国家
senses.definition: a person, country, or place that takes no side, often chosen to host talks
senses.definitionCN: 不选边的人、国家或地点，常被选作会谈地点
senses.example: The talks were held in a neutral, far from both capitals.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈在一个远离两国首都的中立地点举行。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the party that holds the middle position. Recorded as a noun in the mid-15c., it names whoever the balance leaves uncommitted.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指占据中间位置的一方。该名词义在 15 世纪中期已有记录，命名的是被天平留在“未承诺”状态的那一方。

senses.title: Mechanical neutral: no gear engaged
senses.titleCN: 机械空挡：没有齿轮咬合
senses.definition: of a gearbox, in the position where no gear is engaged and no power reaches the wheels
senses.definitionCN: 指变速器处在没有齿轮咬合、动力不传到车轮的位置
senses.example: He shifted into neutral and let the car roll to a stop.
senses.exampleCN: 他挂入空挡，让车滑行到停下。
senses.why: In a gearbox the middle position transmits nothing: neither forward nor reverse. The sense, recorded from 1905, is the balance image in metal.
senses.whyCN: 在变速器里，中间位置什么也不传递：既不前进也不后退。该义项记录于 1905 年，是平衡意象在金属中的版本。

senses.title: Grammatical neuter: neither masculine nor feminine
senses.titleCN: 语法中性：既非阳性也非阴性
senses.definition: in grammar, of a gender that is neither masculine nor feminine
senses.definitionCN: 在语法中，指既非阳性也非阴性的性
senses.example: Latin bellum, meaning war, is a neuter noun.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁语 bellum（战争）是一个中性名词。
senses.why: Latin neuter means 'neither the one nor the other of two'. Grammar applies that either-or refusal to gender, so a noun can stand outside the pair.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 neuter 意为“两者皆非”。语法把这种“两个都不是”的拒绝用在性上，于是名词可以站在这对选项之外。

senses.title: Neutral tone: plain and non-committal
senses.definition: of language or manner, plain and without emotion, giving nothing away
senses.definitionCN: 指语言或态度平实、不带情绪，不透露立场
senses.example: She answered in a neutral tone that gave nothing away.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一种不露声色的中性语气回答。
senses.why: A neutral colour commits to no hue, and a neutral tone commits to no side. The same middle position is applied to speech.
senses.whyCN: 中性色不对任何色相表态，中性语气也不对任何一方表态。同一个“中间位置”被用到了言语上。

intro.en: Neutral is recorded in the 1540s, first in alchemy for a balance of opposing elements, and almost at once for a person who takes no side. Latin neutralis goes back to neuter 'neither the one nor the other', probably a calque of Greek oudeteros.
intro.cn: neutral 记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，最初用于炼金术中对立元素的平衡，几乎同时就用于不选边的人。拉丁语 neutralis 可追溯至 neuter“两者皆非”，很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

items.en: First recorded in the 1540s in alchemy, for a substance in which opposing elements balance, and for the sense 'not taking sides'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，用于炼金术中对立元素相衡的物质，同时也有“不选边”义。

items.en: By the 1550s the word is used of persons who do not join either party in a quarrel.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪 50 年代，这个词已用于不加入争吵任何一方的人。

items.en: Latin neutralis comes from neuter 'neither the one nor the other, neither of two': ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two'. It is probably a calque of Greek oudeteros.
items.cn: 拉丁语 neutralis 来自 neuter“两者皆非、两者都不是”：ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”。它很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

items.en: The two parts are PIE *ne- 'not' and the stem behind uter 'either', which is related to English whether.
items.cn: 两个部分分别是原始印欧语 *ne-“不”与 uter“两者之一”背后的词干，后者与英语 whether 同源。

items.en: Chemistry adopts the word in the 1660s for 'neither acid nor alkaline'; the sense 'not a belligerent' follows in 1711 and the colour sense in 1821.
items.cn: 化学在 17 世纪 60 年代采用这个词，表示“非酸非碱”；“非交战国”义随后于 1711 年出现，颜色义于 1821 年出现。

items.en: The noun is recorded in the mid-15c.; mechanical neutral appears in 1905, and the neutral particle the neutron takes the word into physics.
items.cn: 名词义在 15 世纪中期已有记录；机械空挡义出现于 1905 年，而中性粒子 neutron 把这个词带进了物理学。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and scientific kinship, the second for the idea of not taking a side.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写与科学上的亲缘关系挑选，第二组按“不选边”的意思挑选。

entries.definition: grammatically neither masculine nor feminine. It is the Latin source word neuter, from which neutralis was formed.
entries.definitionCN: 语法上既非阳性也非阴性的。它就是拉丁语源词 neuter，neutralis 由它构成。

entries.definition: existing in nature, not made by people. It starts from Latin natura 'birth', not from neuter.
entries.definitionCN: 自然的；天生的。它来自拉丁语 natura“出生”，不是来自 neuter。

entries.definition: a particle with no electric charge. Its name was coined from neutral plus -on.
entries.definitionCN: 不带电的粒子。它的名字由 neutral 加 -on 造出。

entries.definition: not favouring one side unfairly. It judges fairly between parties, while neutral can also mean simply staying out.
entries.definitionCN: 公正的；不偏不倚的。它在两方之间公正判断，而 neutral 也可以只是置身事外。

entries.definition: showing no interest or concern. It describes unconcern, while neutral describes a balanced position between sides.
entries.definitionCN: 漠不关心的。它描述的是不关心，而 neutral 描述的是在两方之间的平衡位置。

entries.definition: of a state, not formally allied to any major power bloc. It is a political term, narrower than neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 不结盟的。它指国家不正式加入任何大国集团，是政治术语，范围比 neutral 窄。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: ne- plus uter inside neuter, the Latin source neutralis, and the dated scientific senses that followed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：neuter 内部的 ne- 加 uter、拉丁语来源 neutralis，以及随后有年代可查的科学义项。

normal.en: ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two' makes 'neither of the two': the middle position is built into the word.
normal.cn: ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”就是“两者皆非”：中间位置被造进了这个词里。

normal.en: Alchemy gave the first sense, a balance of opposing elements; chemistry kept the picture as neither acid nor alkaline.
normal.cn: 炼金术给了第一个义项，即对立元素的平衡；化学保留这幅画，表示非酸非碱。

normal.en: A neutral country and a neutral referee hold the same spot: outside the two sides.
normal.cn: 中立国与中立裁判站的是同一个位置：在两方之外。

normal.en: Neutral grey commits to no hue, just as a neutral tone commits to no opinion.
normal.cn: 中性灰不对任何色相表态，正如中性语气不对任何观点表态。

normal.en: A gearbox in neutral transmits nothing: the balance image appears again in metal.
normal.cn: 处于空挡的变速器什么也不传递：平衡意象又一次出现在金属里。

abstract.en: A tug-of-war rope whose red marker hangs exactly on the centre line: both teams pull, the marker stays.
abstract.cn: 拔河绳上的红布恰好停在中心线上：两队都在拉，红布不动。

abstract.en: Two arrows pushing a ball from opposite sides with equal force: the ball does not move.
abstract.cn: 两支箭头从相反方向用同样的力推一个球：球不移动。

abstract.en: A switch resting in the middle between on and off: no current, no direction, no commitment.
abstract.cn: 一个停在“开”与“关”正中的开关：没有电流、没有方向、没有承诺。

examples.en: The mediator remained neutral even when one side raised its voice.
examples.cn: 即使一方提高了嗓门，调解人仍然保持中立。

examples.en: Choose a neutral wall colour so the furniture can change later.
examples.cn: 选一种中性的墙面颜色，以后换家具也容易搭配。

examples.en: The country declared itself neutral at the start of the war.
examples.cn: 这个国家在战争开始时宣布中立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛戳」——牛站在两方中间，哪边都不戳、不顶 → neutral 中立的、中性的

root: 源自拉丁语 neutralis，来自 neuter“两者皆非”＝ ne-“不”＋ uter“两者之一”；uter 与 whether 同源，很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of neutral all come from a single position: exactly in the middle, committed to neither side. Alchemy applied it to elements, politics to parties, chemistry to acids, physics to charge, grammar to gender, and speech to tone.
sensesIntro.cn: neutral 的十个义项都来自同一个位置：恰在正中，不属于任何一边。炼金术把它用在元素上，政治用在阵营上，化学用在酸碱上，物理用在电荷上，语法用在性上，言语用在语气上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tug-of-war marker stopped exactly on the centre line.
core.cn: 核心意象：拔河绳上的标记恰好停在中心线上。

branches.en: THE BALANCED MIDDLE: opposing elements in alchemy, and opposing parties in a dispute.
branches.cn: 平衡的中间：炼金术中的对立元素，以及争端中的对立两方。

branches.en: SCIENTIFIC NEUTRALITY: neither acid nor alkaline, and no net electric charge.
branches.cn: 科学上的中性：非酸非碱，以及净电荷为零。

branches.en: THE UNCOMMITTED PARTY: a state outside a war, and the person or place chosen to host talks.
branches.cn: 未承诺的一方：战争之外的国家，以及被选作会谈地点的人或地方。

branches.en: THE QUIET SURFACE: low-saturation colour, and a tone that gives nothing away.
branches.cn: 安静的表层：低彩度的颜色，以及不透露立场的语气。

branches.en: NEITHER ENGAGED NOR EITHER: a gearbox in neutral, and a grammatical gender outside the pair.
branches.cn: 既不咬合也不属于任何一边：空挡的变速器，以及跳出阴阳两性的语法中性。

intro.en: Neutral is Latin neutralis plus -al, from neuter. English builds neutrality, neutrally, neutralize, neutralization, neutralist and neutralism, and the same stem gives neuter and neutron.
intro.cn: neutral 是拉丁语 neutralis 加 -al，源自 neuter。英语构造出 neutrality、neutrally、neutralize、neutralization、neutralist、neutralism，同一词干还给出 neuter 与 neutron。

latinIntro.en: Latin neutralis 'of the neuter gender, neutral' comes from neuter 'neither of two', itself ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 neutralis“中性的、中立的”来自 neuter“两者皆非”，后者由 ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”构成。

items.meaning: taking no side; neither one nor the other
items.meaningCN: 中立的；中性的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The village stayed neutral during the dispute.
items.exampleCN: 争端期间这个村子保持中立。

items.meaning: the state of taking no side
items.meaningCN: 中立；中性（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The treaty guaranteed the neutrality of the port.
items.exampleCN: 条约保障了该港口的中立地位。

items.meaningCN: 中立地；平淡地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She described the quarrel neutrally, naming no culprit.
items.exampleCN: 她中立地描述了这场争吵，没有指名任何一方。

items.meaning: to cancel the effect of something
items.meaningCN: 使中和；抵消（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The base neutralizes the acid almost instantly.

items.meaning: the act of cancelling or balancing
items.meaningCN: 中和作用；抵消（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The neutralization produced ordinary salt and water.
items.exampleCN: 中和反应生成了普通的盐和水。

items.meaningCN: 中立主义者（-ist 构成人名名词）
items.example: The neutralists opposed joining either alliance.
items.exampleCN: 中立主义者反对加入任何一个联盟。

items.meaning: the policy of staying outside rival blocs
items.meaningCN: 中立主义（-ism 构成主张名词）
items.example: Neutralism shaped the country's foreign policy.
items.exampleCN: 中立主义塑造了该国的外交政策。

items.meaningCN: 中性的；既非阳也非阴（ne-“不”+ uter“两者之一”）
items.example: The Latin word for leaf is neuter.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语中“叶子”这个词是中性名词。

items.meaning: a particle with no electric charge
items.meaningCN: 中子（neutral 加粒子后缀 -on，指不带电的粒子）
items.example: A neutron passes through the electric field undeflected.
items.exampleCN: 中子穿过电场时不发生偏转。

items.meaningCN: 中和剂；抵消物（-er 构成施动物名词）
items.example: The lab keeps a neutralizer beside every acid bath.
items.exampleCN: 实验室在每个酸槽旁都放一瓶中和剂。

latinEntries.meaning: neither the one nor the other

latinEntries.meaningCN: 两者之一（与英语 whether 同源）

definition_zh: 分析；解析；化验；对（句子）作语法分析；解析（数据）
definition_en: to separate something into its parts in order to understand or explain it, or to examine a substance, sentence, or set of data in detail
core_image: 拿一把小刀，把复杂的整块事物切成可以单片查看的薄片
scene: 学生在阅览室里摊开一份冗长的实验报告。 She began to analyze the numbers row by row before writing a word.
sceneCN: 这里 analyze 是「分析、解析」（第 1 个义项：把整体拆成部分来理解）；句意为她一个词还没写，就先一行一行地分析这些数字。桌上可见报告、铅笔与计算器。

pos.zh: 动词：分析；解析；化验；对句子作语法分析

derivatives.zh: 由动词逆构回名词，义为「分析；解析；化验」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「分析器；分析者」
由同一词干加 -ist 构成，义为「分析师」
由词干加 -ic 构成，义为「分析的」
analytic 加 -al 构成，义为「分析性的」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可分析的」

senses.title: To break something down in order to understand it
senses.titleCN: 分析：拆开复杂事物以理解它
senses.definition: to separate a complex thing into its parts and study how those parts work together
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂事物分成各个部分，并研究这些部分如何共同运作
senses.example: We need to analyze the causes of the failure before blaming anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 在责怪任何人之前，我们需要分析失败的原因。
senses.why: The verb is the action behind analysis: the whole is loosened until the parts can be handled one at a time.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 analysis 背后的动作：把整体松开，直到各个部分能被一件一件处理。

senses.title: To test a substance in a laboratory
senses.definition: to examine a substance chemically or medically in order to discover what it contains
senses.definitionCN: 用化学或医学方法检测物质，以查明其成分
senses.example: The lab will analyze the soil for heavy metals.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室将检测土壤中的重金属。
senses.why: Laboratory analysis is the same cutting movement applied to matter: the sample is resolved into measurable ingredients.
senses.whyCN: 实验室分析是把同样的「切分」用在物质上：样品被分解成可测量的成分。

senses.title: To treat a patient psychoanalytically
senses.titleCN: 作精神分析：梳理被压抑的心理内容
senses.definition: to treat a person by bringing buried feelings and memories into conscious awareness
senses.definitionCN: 通过把被压抑的情绪与记忆带入意识来治疗一个人
senses.example: The therapist analyzed him twice a week for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗师每周为他做两次精神分析，持续了一年。
senses.why: The mind is treated as a whole that must be loosened: hidden material is separated out and named.
senses.whyCN: 心灵被当作需要松开的整体：隐藏的材料被分离出来并加以命名。

senses.title: To parse a sentence
senses.titleCN: 作语法分析：拆解句子成分
senses.definition: to divide a sentence into its grammatical parts and describe how they fit together
senses.definitionCN: 把句子分成语法成分，并说明它们如何组合
senses.example: The class analyzed the sentence clause by clause.
senses.exampleCN: 全班把这个句子一个从句一个从句地分析。
senses.why: Grammar repeats the same gesture on language: a sentence is cut at its joints so the structure shows.
senses.whyCN: 语法在语言上重复同一个动作：沿句子的关节切开，让结构显形。

senses.title: To process data or code
senses.titleCN: 解析：对数据或代码作计算处理
senses.definition: to examine data or program code systematically, often with a machine, in order to extract meaning or structure
senses.definitionCN: 系统地检查数据或程序代码，常借助机器，以提取意义或结构
senses.example: The software analyzes every message for hidden patterns.
senses.exampleCN: 这个软件会分析每条信息，寻找隐藏的模式。
senses.why: Modern machines perform the old gesture at great speed: they take a stream apart into fields and tokens.
senses.whyCN: 现代机器以极快的速度执行这个古老动作：把数据流拆成字段与标记。

intro.en: Analyze is the verb built beside analysis, and both trace back to the Greek image of loosening something apart.
intro.cn: analyze 是与 analysis 并生的动词，两者都回到希腊语「把某物松开」的意象。

items.en: Analyein meant 'to loosen up, dissolve', from ana- 'up, apart' and lyein 'to loosen'.
items.cn: analyein 意为「松开、溶解」，由 ana-「向上、分开」与 lyein「松开」构成。

items.en: Latin took the noun analysis from Greek; the verb was later formed within the scholarly languages of Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入名词 analysis；动词则是在欧洲学术语言中后来形成的。

items.en: French analyser supplied a model for the English verb, which appears in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语 analyser 为英语动词提供了样板，英语动词见于十七世纪。

items.en: British English settled on analyse, with the -ise ending shared by many learned verbs.
items.cn: 英式英语固定为 analyse，采用许多学术动词共有的 -ise 结尾。

items.en: American spelling prefers analyze, with -yze, following a pattern also seen in paralyze.
items.cn: 美式拼写偏好 analyze，用 -yze，这一模式也见于 paralyze。

items.en: The verb now ranges from chemistry to grammar to computing, but each use still cuts a whole into readable parts.
items.cn: 这个动词如今从化学延伸到语法与计算，但每种用法仍在把整体切成可读的部分。

note.en: The look-alike group is the analysis family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of close inspection that differ in method.
note.cn: 形近组是 analysis 词族；近义组收仔细检查类动词，方法各有不同。

entries.definition: The noun naming the act or result of breaking something into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指把事物分成部分的行为或结果。

entries.definition: A person who analyzes data or samples professionally.
entries.definitionCN: 以分析数据或样品为职业的人。

entries.definition: An adjective for a method that separates things into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指把事物分成部分的方法。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning skilled at analysis or produced by it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「善于分析的」或「经分析得出的」。

entries.definition: To look at something closely, often without taking it apart.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细查看某物，通常并不把它拆开。

entries.definition: To cut a body or an argument apart in order to study its parts.
entries.definitionCN: 把身体或论点切开，以研究其各部分。

entries.definition: To explain what something means rather than how it is built.
entries.definitionCN: 解释某物的含义，而非它的构造。

entries.definition: To judge the value or quality of something after examining it.
entries.definitionCN: 在考察之后判断某物的价值或质量。

normalIntro.en: The hooks below link the verb to the noun, to its spelling and to the physical act of cutting something open.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子把这个动词与名词、拼写以及「切开」的实体动作连起来。

normal.en: Analyze is what an analyst does with an analysis: three forms, one job.
normal.cn: analyze 是 analyst 用 analysis 做的事：三个形式，一份工作。

normal.en: The British version swaps the z for an s: analyse looks softer, analyze sharper.
normal.cn: 英式版本把 z 换成 s：analyse 看着更软，analyze 看着更利。

normal.en: Picture a lab technician slicing a sample into thin sections on a glass slide.
normal.cn: 想象实验员把样品切成薄片，放在玻璃载玻片上。

normal.en: The stress is on the second syllable, so the word itself sounds like a decision being made.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节，读起来像正在下一个判断。

normal.en: You analyze data, a sentence, or a feeling; the verb always wants an object.
normal.cn: 你可以 analyze 数据、句子或情绪；这个动词总要带一个宾语。

abstract.en: To analyze is to refuse the comfort of a first impression.
abstract.cn: 分析就是拒绝第一印象带来的舒适。

abstract.en: Every analysis begins with the admission that the obvious reading is not the whole story.
abstract.cn: 每次分析都始于承认：显而易见的读法并不是全部。

abstract.en: Analysis is patience turned into a method.
abstract.cn: 分析是把耐心变成一种方法。

examples.en: Researchers analyze thousands of samples every month.
examples.cn: 研究人员每个月分析数千份样品。

examples.en: Before you analyze the poem, read it aloud once.
examples.cn: 在分析这首诗之前，先大声读一遍。

examples.en: The program can analyze the logs faster than any person.
examples.cn: 这个程序能比任何人更快地解析日志。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安拿来试」：安安静静拿过来试一试，一样一样拆开看。

root: 希腊语 ana-（向上、分开）+ lyein（松开），动词义即「把整体松开、拆散」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with general understanding, then specializes into chemical testing, psychotherapy, grammar and machine parsing.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从一般的理解出发，再分化为化验、心理治疗、语法分析与机器解析。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade moves through a complex whole so that each layer can be looked at separately.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃穿过复杂的整体，让每一层都能被单独查看。

branches.en: THE GENERAL ACT: the first sense is plain understanding by separation.
branches.cn: 一般动作线：第一个义项就是通过分离来理解。

branches.en: THE SAMPLE: the second sense cuts into matter and reads its composition.
branches.cn: 样品线：第二个义项切进物质，读出它的组成。

branches.en: THE MIND: the third sense cuts into memory and feeling.
branches.cn: 心灵线：第三个义项切进记忆与情绪。

branches.en: THE SENTENCE: the fourth sense cuts language at its grammatical joints.
branches.cn: 句子线：第四个义项沿语法关节切开语言。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: the fifth sense makes the cutting automatic and fast.
branches.cn: 机器线：第五个义项让切开变得自动而迅速。

intro.en: The verb and its noun share one Greek stem, and English adds suffixes to mark person, instrument and possibility.
intro.cn: 动词与名词共享一个希腊词干，英语再加后缀标示人物、工具与可能性。

latinIntro.en: The family is built with -sis, -st, -er, -ic, -al and -able around the stem analy-.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族以 analy- 为核心，用 -sis、-st、-er、-ic、-al、-able 扩展。

items.meaning: the act or result of separating a whole
items.meaningCN: 把整体分开的行为或结果
items.example: The analysis took longer than the experiment.
items.exampleCN: 分析比实验本身花的时间还长。

items.example: She works as a data analyst.

items.meaning: a device or person that analyzes
items.example: The analyzer broke down each frequency.
items.exampleCN: 分析仪把每个频率分解开来。
他有一颗分析型的头脑。

items.example: The essay is analytical, not descriptive.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章是分析性的，不是描述性的。
她以分析的方式处理这个问题。

items.example: The recording is noisy but analyzable.
items.exampleCN: 录音有噪声，但仍可分析。

items.example: Much of the evidence remains unanalyzed.
items.exampleCN: 许多证据仍未得到分析。

definition_zh: 部分；一份（食物）；应得的份额；命运；（动词）分配
definition_en: a part or share of something larger; an amount of food served to one person; to divide something into shares
core_image: 把一整块切开，把属于你的那一份放到你面前
scene: 每位客人都分到了满满一份烤肉。 Each guest received a generous portion of the roast.
sceneCN: 这里 portion 是「分给一个人的一份食物」（第 2 个义项：一份）；句意：每位客人都分到了一份量很足的烤肉。场景要点：整块被切开、按人分、放在各自盘里；对应第 1 个义项。

collocations.zh: 最大的一份（源自狮子分猎物的典故）

derivatives.zh: 没有份额的；无嫁妆的（古）

senses.title: A part of a whole
senses.definition: a part of a larger whole, especially one separated or regarded separately
senses.definitionCN: 一个更大整体中的一部分，尤指被分开或单独看待的那部分
senses.example: A large portion of the budget goes to salaries.
senses.exampleCN: 预算中很大一部分用于工资。
senses.why: Latin portio meant a share assigned to someone. The word begins with the act of cutting a whole and handing out pieces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 portio 意为“分派给某人的一份”。这个词起于这样一个动作：把整体切开，再把块分出去。

senses.title: A serving of food
senses.titleCN: 一份（食物）：放到你盘里的量
senses.definition: the amount of food served to one person at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次盛给一个人的食物量
senses.example: Each guest received a generous portion of the roast.
senses.exampleCN: 每位客人都分到了一份量很足的烤肉。
senses.why: Food is the most everyday whole that gets divided. The share on your plate is a portion in the most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 食物是最日常的被分割的整体。你盘里的那一份，就是最具体的 portion。

senses.title: An allotted share of property
senses.titleCN: 应得份额：法律上分给你的那一份
senses.definition: the share of an estate or property that is assigned to a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 遗产或财产中分配给某个特定人的份额
senses.example: She received her portion of the family land at twenty-one.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十一岁时得到了属于自己的那份家族土地。
senses.why: Inheritance makes the metaphor legal: the whole is fixed, the shares are named, and each heir gets a portion.
senses.whyCN: 继承把这个比喻法律化了：整体是固定的，份额是有名分的，每个继承人各得一份。

senses.title: One's lot or fate
senses.titleCN: 命运：分给一生的那一份
senses.definition: the share of life, good or bad, that a person is given, in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 文学用语，指一个人被分得的那一份人生，无论好坏
senses.example: He accepted his portion of suffering without complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫无怨言地接受了分给自己的那份苦难。
senses.why: If goods can be allotted, so can experiences. Life itself becomes a whole divided among people, and yours is your portion.
senses.whyCN: 如果财物可以被分派，经历也可以。人生本身成了一个分给众人的整体，你的那一份就是你的 portion。

senses.title: To divide into shares
senses.definition: to divide something into shares and give them out
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成若干份并发给各人
senses.example: The committee portioned the funds among the three projects.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会把资金分给了三个项目。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act that produced it: to portion is to perform the cutting and handing out.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成产生它的那个动作：to portion 就是执行“切开并分发”这件事。

senses.title: To provide with a dowry
senses.titleCN: 给嫁妆：旧时按份给女儿财产
senses.definition: in older usage, to give a daughter a dowry or a share of property at marriage
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指在女儿出嫁时给她嫁妆或一份财产
senses.example: The will portioned his daughters before his sons.
senses.exampleCN: 遗嘱先给女儿们分好了嫁妆，然后才轮到儿子。
senses.why: A dowry is literally a daughter's portion, the share set aside for her. The verb records that legal practice.
senses.whyCN: 嫁妆字面就是“女儿的那一份”，即为她单留出来的份额。动词记录的就是这一法律习俗。

senses.title: A section of a larger work
senses.titleCN: 章节：一部作品里的一段
senses.definition: one section of a book, document, or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 书、文件或乐曲中的一个段落
senses.example: Only a small portion of the report deals with costs.
senses.exampleCN: 报告里只有一小部分谈到成本。
senses.why: A text is a whole too. It can be divided into sections, and each section is a portion of the text.
senses.whyCN: 文本也是一个整体，可以被分成段落，每一段就是文本的一个 portion。

senses.title: An allocated amount
senses.titleCN: 配额：按规定量给你的数
senses.definition: a measured amount of something allocated to a person or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 按定量分配给某人或某用途的一份数量
senses.example: The daily portion of grain was weighed out at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 每天那份谷物在黎明时称好分出。
senses.why: When the share is measured rather than simply cut, portion means a fixed quantity: a ration by another name.
senses.whyCN: 当份额是被量出来的而不只是切出来的，portion 就指一个固定数量：换个名字的配给量。

intro.en: Portion comes from a Latin word for an assigned share. The step before it rests on a reconstructed form, so that link is probable rather than directly recorded.
intro.cn: portion 来自拉丁语中表示“分派的份额”的词。它前面的一步建立在重构形式上，因此那一环是“很可能”，而非有直接文献记录。

items.en: Portio meant 'a share, a part, an allotted portion'. It is recorded in classical Latin for shares of property and of food.
items.cn: portio 意为“份额、部分、分得的一份”。古典拉丁语中已用它指财产与食物的份额。

items.en: Portio is generally traced to a reconstructed *partio 'division', related to pars 'part' and ultimately to PIE *pere- (2) 'to grant, allot'. The asterisk marks a form found in no text, so this link is probable rather than documented.
items.cn: portio 一般被追溯到重构形式 *partio“划分”，与 pars“部分”相关，并可再上溯到原始印欧语 *pere- (2)“分配、给予”。星号表示这个形式不见于任何文献，所以这一环是“很可能”，而非有据可查。

items.en: Old French took the Latin accusative portionem and shaped it as porcion, meaning a share or a part.
items.cn: 古法语取拉丁语宾格 portionem，改造为 porcion，意为一份或一部分。

items.en: English borrowed porcion in the early 14th century. Early uses are legal and religious: a share of an estate, a share of goods, an assigned lot in life.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪初借入 porcion。早期用法多属法律与宗教：遗产的一份、财物的一份、被分得的人生际遇。

items.en: The everyday sense 'amount of food for one person' develops later and becomes dominant in modern usage, especially in restaurants and diet advice.
items.cn: “一人份食物量”这一日常义发展较晚，却在现代用法中占据主导，尤其在餐饮与饮食建议里。

items.en: The verb appears alongside the noun, and compounds such as apportion and proportion extend the family. All of them keep the picture of cutting a whole into shares.
items.cn: 动词与名词并行出现，apportion、proportion 等复合词扩展了这个词族。它们都保留了“把整体切成份”的画面。

note.en: The first group is built by adding prefixes to portion itself. The second group collects words for parts and shares.
note.cn: 第一组是在 portion 本身前面加前缀构成。第二组收表示“部分与份额”的词。

entries.definition: to divide and assign in due shares. Ad- 'to' plus portion: to give each their portion.
entries.definitionCN: 按应得的份额划分并分配。ad-“向”加 portion：给每个人应得的那一份。

entries.definition: a relation between parts, or a balanced share. Pro- 'in relation to' plus portion gives the idea of shares measured against each other.
entries.definitionCN: 部分之间的关系，或均衡的份额。pro-“相对”加 portion，给出“份额互相比量”的意思。

entries.definition: changing in a fixed ratio with something else. It extends proportion with -al.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一事物按固定比率变化的。它由 proportion 加 -al 扩展而来。

entries.definition: having no share, especially no dowry. Portion plus -less, common in older legal and literary texts.
entries.definitionCN: 没有份额的，尤指没有嫁妆。portion 加 -less，多见于较早的法律与文学文本。

entries.definition: a piece of a whole. Part is the broad neutral word; portion adds the idea of a share assigned to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一块。part 是宽泛中性的词；portion 多出“分配给某人的份额”之意。

entries.definition: a part belonging to or owed to a person. Share matches portion in legal and financial contexts and is more common there.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某人或应归某人的一部分。share 在法律与财务语境中与 portion 相当，且更常用。

entries.definition: an amount of food for one person. Serving is the everyday restaurant word; portion also carries the sense of an allotted share.
entries.definitionCN: 供一个人吃的食物量。serving 是餐馆日常用语；portion 还带有“分得的份额”之意。

entries.definition: an amount officially given out. Allotment stresses official distribution; portion can be informal or literary.
entries.definitionCN: 官方分发的数量。allotment 强调官方分配；portion 可以是非正式的或文学性的。

entries.definition: a fixed allowance of something scarce. Ration implies shortage and control; portion does not.
entries.definitionCN: 对稀缺物资的固定配给量。ration 含短缺与管制之意；portion 不含。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the slice on the plate, the inheritance, the measured grain, the prefix family, and the fate you are dealt.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：盘里的那一块、遗产里的那一份、量出来的谷物、前缀家族、分给你的一生。

normal.en: Picture a whole roast cut into slices. The slice on your plate is your portion.
normal.cn: 想象一整块烤肉被切成片。你盘里的那一片就是你的 portion。

normal.en: Portion out means hand each person their slice, one by one.
normal.cn: portion out 就是一片一片地把属于各人的那份递过去。

normal.en: In a will, the whole estate is divided and each child gets a portion.
normal.cn: 遗嘱里，整份遗产被切开，每个孩子得到一份 portion。

normal.en: A portion of grain weighed at dawn is a ration under another name.
normal.cn: 黎明时称出的那份谷物，就是换个名字的配给量。

normal.en: Apportion, proportion, portionless: same core, different prefixes and suffixes.
normal.cn: apportion、proportion、portionless：同一个核心，不同的前后缀。

abstract.en: Every whole can be cut, and every cut produces an owner; portion is the word where division becomes possession.
abstract.cn: 每个整体都可被切开，每次切开都产生一个所有者；portion 正是“分割变成占有”的那个词。

abstract.en: A portion is a boundary drawn inside a thing, and boundaries are always drawn by someone.
abstract.cn: 一份是在事物内部画出的一条界线，而界线总是由某个人画的。

abstract.en: When life is called a portion, the metaphor admits that not everything is available to everyone.
abstract.cn: 当人生被称为一份 portion 时，这个比喻承认了：并非所有东西对所有人都是可得的。

examples.en: Only a small portion of the manuscript has survived.
examples.cn: 这份手稿只有一小部分留存下来。

examples.en: Restaurants here are known for generous portions at low prices.
examples.cn: 这里的餐馆以分量足、价格低闻名。

examples.en: The land was portioned among the villagers after the reform.
examples.cn: 改革之后，土地被分给了村民。

dict_mnemonic.text: “剖心”——把整颗心剖开，分给每人一份，就是 portion（份额）；注意这只是谐音，与词源无关

root: 拉丁语 portio“份额、部分”（一般追溯到重构形式 *partio“划分”，与 pars“部分”相关，来自 PIE *pere- (2)“分配”）→ 古法语 porcion → 英语 portion（14 世纪初）。

sensesIntro.en: The word always involves cutting a whole and assigning a piece. Food, inheritance, text, and even fate are all wholes of different kinds, and the piece assigned to you is your portion. The verb simply performs that cut.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终涉及“把整体切开并指派一块”。食物、遗产、文本乃至命运，都是不同种类的整体，分给你的那一块就是你的 portion。动词则是执行这一刀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole loaf cut at the table, one slice placed before each person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整条面包在桌上被切开，每个面前放上一片。

chain: A PART CUT FROM A WHOLE

branches.en: PART: a piece of any whole, whether a budget or a book.
branches.cn: 部分：任何整体中的一块，无论是预算还是书。

branches.en: MEASURE: the plate and the scale, food and fixed allowance.
branches.cn: 量：盘子与秤，食物与定量。

branches.en: LAW: inheritance shares and the dowry set aside for a daughter.
branches.cn: 法律：继承份额与为女儿单留的嫁妆。

branches.en: FATE: the share of life dealt to a person.
branches.cn: 命运：分给一个人的那份人生。

branches.en: ACTION: the act of cutting and handing out.
branches.cn: 动作：切开并分发的行为。

intro.en: Portion has generated a small family through prefixes that specify direction or relation (to, for, in ratio) and suffixes that make adjectives and verbs.
intro.cn: portion 通过表示方向或关系的前缀（向、为、按比例）以及构成形容词与动词的后缀，衍生出一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun portio and its related verb forms supplied the base; English built the rest with native endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 portio 及其相关动词形式提供了基底；其余部分由英语用本土词尾构造。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 分配者（苏格兰法律用语）

items.meaningCN: 部分（与 portio 关系未证实）

definition_zh: 架子；置物架；使痛苦；齿条；绞尽脑汁
definition_en: a frame with shelves or bars for storing things; to cause great pain or worry; a toothed bar in a machine; to think very hard, in the phrase rack one's brains
core_image: 墙边一排木架，盘子一只只竖插在格子间
scene: 厨房的墙边立着一排木架，盘子一只只竖着插在格子里。 She slid the hot tray onto the rack and stepped back.
sceneCN: 这里 rack 是「架子、置物架」（第 1 个义项：带格栅或层板用来存放物品的框架）；句意为她把滚烫的烤盘放到架子上，然后退后一步。画面里可留意：木架、竖插的盘子、冒着热气的烤盘。

pos.zh: 架子；置物架；行李架；齿条

derivatives.zh: rack 加 -ing，指令人极度痛苦的，如 racking pain
rack 加 -ety，指摇摇晃晃、吵闹破旧的
rack 与 pinion 复合，指齿条与齿轮组成的传动机构

senses.title: A frame for storing things
senses.definition: a frame with shelves, bars or hooks used to hold or store objects
senses.definitionCN: 带层板、横杆或挂钩、用来放置或存放物品的框架
senses.example: Put the plates on the rack to dry.
senses.exampleCN: 把盘子放到架子上晾干。
senses.why: The noun comes from a Germanic word for something stretched out, and a frame of bars is exactly a stretched structure.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自一个日耳曼语词，意为被撑展开的东西，而由横杆构成的框架正是一种被撑开的结构。

senses.title: To cause great pain or worry
senses.definition: to subject someone to severe pain, strain or mental suffering
senses.definitionCN: 使某人遭受剧烈疼痛、拉扯或精神折磨
senses.example: Guilt racked him for years after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后，负罪感折磨了他多年。
senses.why: An older meaning of the verb was to stretch a body on a frame, and from that physical stretching came the sense of extreme suffering.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词较早的意思是把人拉展在刑架上，从这种身体的拉扯生出了极度痛苦的义项。

senses.title: A toothed bar in a machine
senses.definition: a bar with teeth that engages a wheel to turn motion into a straight line
senses.definitionCN: 带齿的杆件，与齿轮啮合，把转动变成直线运动
senses.example: The steering rack turns the wheel's motion into a sideways push.
senses.exampleCN: 转向齿条把方向盘的转动变成横向的推力。
senses.why: The same frame of repeated bars appears in machinery, where a row of teeth on a bar is also called a rack.
senses.whyCN: 同一种由一排横杆构成的形象也出现在机械里，杆上排成一列的齿也被叫作 rack。

senses.title: To think very hard
senses.definition: to search one's memory with great effort, almost always in the phrase rack one's brains
senses.definitionCN: 极用力地在记忆里搜寻，几乎总用于 rack one's brains 这一说法
senses.example: I racked my brains for her name but could not find it.
senses.exampleCN: 我绞尽脑汁想她的名字，却怎么也想不起来。
senses.why: Thinking is pictured as stretching the mind on a frame, the same painful image as the older verb of torment.
senses.whyCN: 思考被想象成把心智在框架上拉展，与较早那个表示折磨的动词是同一幅痛苦的形象。

intro.en: Rack comes from Germanic words for something stretched or drawn out, and both the frame and the torment senses grew from that picture; no reliable Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: rack 来自日耳曼语中表示「被撑开、被拉长之物」的词，架子义与折磨义都从这幅画面生长出来；没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Rec meant a framework or a rack, and related verbs meant to stretch something out.
items.cn: rec 指框架或架子，相关的动词意为把某物撑展开。

items.en: Middle English rakke named a frame of bars, especially one for holding animal feed.
items.cn: 中古英语 rakke 指由横杆构成的框架，尤指盛放饲料的架子。

items.en: A related verb meant to stretch a body on a frame, which produced the sense of severe pain and torment.
items.cn: 一个相关的动词意为把人拉展在框架上，由此产生了剧痛与折磨的义项。

items.en: Machine makers used the same word for a toothed bar, because its teeth look like a row of bars.
items.cn: 机械制造者把同一个词用于带齿的杆件，因为那排齿看起来就像一排横杆。

items.en: Modern English keeps the shelf, the torment, the gear bar and the phrase about racking one's brains.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了置物架、折磨、齿条，以及「绞尽脑汁」这一说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that merely resemble the spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for shelves, frames and torment.
note.cn: 形近组收只是拼写相似的词；近义组收表示架子、框架与折磨的词。

entries.definition: A bat with strings, or a loud confusing noise.
entries.definitionCN: 带弦的球拍，或嘈杂混乱的响声。

entries.definition: Causing severe pain or strain.
entries.definitionCN: 造成剧痛或极度紧张的。

entries.definition: Noisy and rather worn out.
A support fixed to a wall, or a pair of written signs.
entries.definitionCN: 固定在墙上的托架，或一对书写符号。

entries.definition: A flat board fixed to a wall or inside furniture.
entries.definitionCN: 固定在墙上或家具内部的平板。

entries.definition: A structure of bars that supports or surrounds something.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑或围住某物的杆件结构。

entries.definition: Severe lasting pain of body or mind.
entries.definitionCN: 身心上剧烈而持久的痛苦。

entries.definition: Pressure that stretches or damages something.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物被拉扯或受损的压力。

normalIntro.en: One picture holds the word together: something stretched on a frame, whether a shelf, a machine bar or a suffering body.
normalIntro.cn: 一幅画面把这个词连在一起：被撑展在框架上的东西，无论是层架、机械杆件，还是受苦的身体。

normal.en: Rack your brains is the idiom to remember: the mind is imagined as stretched on a frame until an answer appears.
normal.cn: 记住 rack your brains 这个成语：头脑被想象成在框架上拉展，直到答案出现。

normal.en: A luggage rack holds bags overhead, while a wine rack holds bottles on their sides.
normal.cn: luggage rack 在头顶放包，wine rack 让酒瓶横躺着。

normal.en: Racking pain is pain so strong it feels as if the body is being stretched.
normal.cn: racking pain 指强到像身体被拉扯的疼痛。

normal.en: A rack and pinion is a toothed bar and wheel that turn rotation into straight movement.
normal.cn: rack and pinion 是齿条与齿轮，把转动变成直线运动。

normal.en: Go to rack and ruin means to fall into complete decay, as an old frame collapsing.
normal.cn: go to rack and ruin 意为彻底败落，像一副旧框架垮掉。

abstract.en: A shelf and a torture frame share one word because both hold a body in a fixed position.
abstract.cn: 层架与刑架共用一个词，因为两者都把「身体」固定在一个位置上。

abstract.en: Racking one's brains is a small daily version of the old torment: effort applied until something gives.
abstract.cn: 绞尽脑汁是古老折磨的日常小版本：不断施力，直到某样东西松口。

abstract.en: Machines borrow human words, and a toothed bar becomes a rack because it looks like a row of shelves.
abstract.cn: 机器会借用人的词，带齿的杆件因为看起来像一排层架而成了 rack。

examples.en: He hung his coat on the rack by the door.
examples.cn: 他把外套挂在门边的架子上。

examples.en: She racked her brains for a way to explain the delay.
examples.cn: 她绞尽脑汁想找出解释延误的办法。

examples.en: The old shed had gone to rack and ruin.
examples.cn: 那座旧棚子已经彻底破败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞克」——架子一格一格像被拉开，记住 rack 是架子；想不出来就得绞尽脑汁。

root: 中古荷兰语 rec（框架）→ 中古英语 rakke（横杆框架）→ 英语 rack；同族有 racking、rackety、rack-and-pinion。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a stretched frame; the senses divide into a shelf, a machine bar, bodily torment and the effort of thinking.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被撑展的框架」；义项分为层架、机械杆件、身体折磨与用力的思考。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of wooden frames along a kitchen wall, plates standing in the slots.
core.cn: 核心意象：厨房墙边一排木架，盘子竖插在格子里。

branches.en: a hot tray sliding into place
branches.cn: 滑进位置的滚烫烤盘

branches.en: a hand gripping a bar too long
branches.cn: 握杆太久的一只手

branches.en: teeth meeting teeth in a gear
branches.cn: 齿轮上齿与齿相咬

branches.en: a name hunted for and not found
branches.cn: 苦寻而不得的一个名字

branches.en: the same strain, once on the body and once on the mind
branches.cn: 同一种拉扯，一次在身体上，一次在头脑里

intro.en: The word is Germanic in origin and carries its meanings through a short root plus English endings for adjectives and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，靠一个短词根，加上构成形容词与复合词的英语词尾来承载词义。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_zh: 有系统的；有体系的；按部就班的
definition_en: arranged or carried out according to a system
core_image: 档案柜的抽屉依次拉开，每格都贴着同样的标签格式
scene: 他的整理方式很有系统。 His filing method was systematical.
sceneCN: 这里 systematical 是「有系统的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的整理方式很有系统。

senses.title: Arranged as a system
senses.definition: laid out as a connected whole
senses.definitionCN: 按相连整体来安排
senses.example: His filing method was systematical.
senses.exampleCN: 他的整理方式很有系统。
senses.why: This longer form adds -al to systematic, stressing the state of being arranged as a system.
senses.whyCN: 这个较长形式在 systematic 后加 -al，强调被安排成系统的状态。

senses.title: Following set steps
senses.definition: carried out step by step in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序一步步进行
senses.example: The training was systematical from the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 训练从第一天起就按部就班。
senses.why: A system imposes an order of steps, which yields the sense of doing things in sequence.
senses.whyCN: 系统规定了步骤次序，于是产生按部就班之义。

intro.en: Systematical adds the adjective ending -al to systematic.
intro.cn: systematical 是在 systematic 后加形容词词尾 -al 而成。

items.en: Systema meant an organized whole.
items.cn: systema 意为有组织的整体。

items.en: Systematikos meant skilled in arranging.
items.cn: systematikos 意为善于安排。

items.en: Systematic entered English as ordered by method.
items.cn: systematic 以「按方法有序」之义进入英语。

items.en: Systematical added -al to stress the arranged state.
items.cn: systematical 加 -al 以强调被安排的状态。

items.en: Systematical survives mainly as a rarer variant.
items.cn: systematical 主要作为较少见的变体留存。

note.en: Systematical is compared with look-alike words and with words for ordered arrangement.
note.cn: 把 systematical 与形近词以及表示有序安排的词作比较。

entries.definition: done by ordered method
in an ordered way
a set of connected parts
neat and well arranged
having a clear arrangement
careful and ordered

normalIntro.en: Systematical describes things that have been given a system.
normalIntro.cn: systematical 描述已被赋予系统的事物。

normal.en: His filing method was systematical.
normal.cn: 他的整理方式很有系统。

normal.en: The training was systematical from the first day.
normal.cn: 训练从第一天起就按部就班。

normal.en: She kept a systematical record of every lesson.
normal.cn: 她为每节课做系统记录。

normal.en: The course offers a systematical study of grammar.
normal.cn: 这门课提供系统的语法学习。

normal.en: Their approach was systematical rather than random.
normal.cn: 他们的方法有系统，而非随意。

abstract.en: Systematical is order made into a habit.
abstract.cn: 有系统就是把秩序变成习惯。

abstract.en: A systematical mind leaves nothing to chance.
abstract.cn: 有系统的头脑不把任何事交给偶然。

abstract.en: Structure outside calms the noise inside.
abstract.cn: 外在的结构能平息内在的嘈杂。

examples.en: His filing method was systematical.

examples.en: The course offers a systematical study of grammar.

examples.cn: 他们的方法有系统，而非随意。

dict_mnemonic.text: systematical 是 systematic 加 -al 的较长变体，意思相同，都表示有系统、按部就班。

root: 由 systematic 加形容词词尾 -al 构成，最终源自希腊语 systema（有组织的整体）。

sensesIntro.en: Systematical means arranged as a system, or carried out step by step.
sensesIntro.cn: systematical 表示按系统安排，或一步步执行。

core.en: Order that has been built into the way things are kept.
core.cn: 秩序已被建入事物的存放方式。

branches.en: His filing method was systematical.
branches.cn: 他的整理方式很有系统。

branches.en: She kept a systematical record of every lesson.
branches.cn: 她为每节课做系统记录。

branches.en: The training was systematical from the first day.

branches.en: The course offers a systematical study of grammar.

branches.en: Their approach was systematical rather than random.

intro.en: Systematical forms systematically and is a variant of systematic.
intro.cn: systematical 可构成 systematically，是 systematic 的变体。

latinIntro.en: The -al ending is Latin; Latin ordo, order, underlies the meaning.
latinIntro.cn: -al 词尾源自拉丁语；其含义根植于拉丁语 ordo（次序）。

definition_zh: 诅咒；咒骂；祸根；祸因
definition_en: to call down harm on someone in words, or a cause of lasting trouble
core_image: 老人对着门槛啐一口，低声吐出一串狠话
scene: 老太太对着门槛啐了一口，低声念出一串难听的话。 She cursed the man who had cheated her.
sceneCN: 这里 cursed 是 curse 的过去式，指「咒骂」（第 2 个义项：用难听的话发泄怒气）；句意是她咒骂那个骗过她的人。

senses.title: Words that wish harm
senses.definition: words spoken to bring harm or bad luck upon someone
senses.definitionCN: 为把伤害或厄运带给某人而说出的话
senses.example: The old woman muttered a curse at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 老妇人在门口低声念了一句诅咒。
senses.why: Words are the cheapest weapon, and the hardest to recall.
senses.whyCN: 话是最便宜的武器，也最难收回。

senses.title: To swear at
senses.definition: to say angry, rude words about someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 用愤怒粗鲁的话骂某人或某事
senses.example: He cursed the driver who splashed him.
senses.exampleCN: 他咒骂那个溅了他一身水的司机。
senses.why: Anger looks for a target and finds one in words.
senses.whyCN: 怒气总要找一个目标，于是在话里找到了。

senses.title: A cause of trouble
senses.definition: something that brings great and lasting trouble
senses.definitionCN: 带来巨大而持久麻烦的事物
senses.example: That old car became a curse for the family.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧车成了这家的祸根。
senses.why: A thing can weigh on a life the way a spell is said to.
senses.whyCN: 一件东西压在生活上，就像传说里的咒语一样。

intro.en: Curse comes from Old English cursian, to utter words that wish harm; its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: curse 源自古英语 cursian（说出希望别人遭殃的话），更早的来源已不可确考。

items.en: Cursian meant to speak words that wish harm.
items.cn: cursian 意为说出希望别人遭殃的话。

items.en: The noun curs named such a spoken wish.
items.cn: 名词 curs 指这样一句说出口的恶愿。

items.en: Curs spread from church curses to everyday swearing.
items.cn: curs 从教会的诅咒扩展到日常骂人。

items.en: It also named a person or thing that brings ruin.
items.cn: 它也指带来毁灭的人或物。

items.en: Curse keeps both the formal spell and the casual swear.
items.cn: curse 同时保留了正式的咒语和随口的骂话。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cur- opening, and the meaning group names other ways of wishing harm.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cur- 开头，近义组列出其他表达恶愿的说法。

entries.definition: a path or a series of lessons
a line that bends smoothly
to swear in casual speech
to use rude words in anger
to condemn someone to punishment
a spell meant to bring bad luck

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a word spat at a doorstep and end with a thing nobody can get rid of.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从门槛上啐出的一句话开始，落到一件谁也甩不掉的东西上。

normal.en: A curse is anger given grammar and aimed.
normal.cn: 诅咒就是给怒气装上语法，再瞄准。

normal.en: The same word covers a witch's spell and a driver's bad language.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指巫师的咒语，也指司机的脏话。

normal.en: A curse is said to follow a family for generations.
normal.cn: 据说诅咒会跟着一个家族走好几代。

normal.en: When a thing ruins every year, people call it a curse.
normal.cn: 当一样东西年年坏事，人们就叫它祸根。

normal.en: You can lift a curse, but not the words already heard.
normal.cn: 诅咒可以解除，已经听进耳朵的话却收不回。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised at a doorway in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中有人在门口举起一只手。

abstract.en: Picture a mouth shaping words that nobody wants to hear.
abstract.cn: 想象一张嘴正在拼出谁也不愿听的话。

abstract.en: Picture an old car that breaks down every winter.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆每年冬天都要坏一次的旧车。

examples.en: The old woman muttered a curse at the door.
examples.cn: 老妇人在门口低声念了一句诅咒。

examples.en: He cursed the driver who splashed him.
examples.cn: 他咒骂那个溅了他一身水的司机。

examples.en: That old car became a curse for the family.
examples.cn: 那辆旧车成了这家的祸根。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 curse 记成「啐」：对着人啐一口，再吐出一串狠话，就是诅咒。

root: 源自古英语 cursian（说出希望别人遭殃的话），名词形式为 curs；本义是用言语祈求他人受害，后来引申为骂人，再引申为带来持久麻烦的祸根。

sensesIntro.en: From words that wish harm, to angry swearing, to a thing that ruins a life.
sensesIntro.cn: 从祈求别人遭殃的话，到愤怒的骂声，再到毁掉生活的祸根。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised at a doorway while hard words are spoken.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人在门口举起手，嘴里吐出狠话。

branches.en: The oldest picture is a spoken wish for harm.
branches.cn: 最古老的画面，是一句说出口的恶愿。

branches.en: The same act appears when anger simply needs to swear.
branches.cn: 当怒气只是想骂出来时，出现的是同一种动作。

branches.en: A thing that ruins a life is felt to be under a spell.
branches.cn: 毁掉生活的东西，让人觉得像中了咒。

branches.en: A solemn spell and a casual swear are the same words in different clothes.
branches.cn: 庄重的咒语和随口的脏话，是同一批话换了衣服。

branches.en: Swearing at a thing turns it into the enemy in the house.
branches.cn: 骂一样东西，就把它变成了屋里的敌人。

intro.en: Curse is an Old English word with a small family, all of it built on spoken harm.
intro.cn: curse 是古英语词，词族不大，全都围绕「说出口的伤害」建成。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin root; it comes from Old English cursian.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 cursian。

items.example: She cursed him under her breath.
They believed the house was cursed.

那该诅咒的噪音一刻不停。

items.meaning: a rude word used in anger

items.meaning: to place a spell on someone
items.example: The story says she put a curse on the well.
items.exampleCN: 故事说她给那口井下了咒。

items.example: Only a kind act could lift the curse.
items.exampleCN: 只有善举才能解除诅咒。

definition_zh: 容器；集装箱
definition_en: a box, bottle or other object made to hold things
core_image: 码头上一排巨大的彩色集装箱
scene: 码头上，吊机把一只铁箱从船上吊到卡车。 The container was loaded with clothes.
sceneCN: 这里 container 指「集装箱」（第 2 个义项：运输货物用的大铁箱）；句意是这只集装箱装满了衣服。

senses.title: A holder for things
senses.definition: a box, jar or bottle used to hold food or objects
senses.definitionCN: 用来盛放食物或物品的盒、罐或瓶
senses.example: Keep the flour in a dry container.
senses.exampleCN: 把面粉放在干燥的容器里。
senses.why: Small loose things need one shell to become a load.
senses.whyCN: 零散的小东西需要一个外壳，才能变成一批货。

senses.title: A giant steel box
senses.definition: a very large metal box used for moving goods by ship or train
senses.definitionCN: 用船或火车运送货物的大型金属箱
senses.example: The container left the port at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那只集装箱在黎明时驶离港口。
senses.why: Standard sizes turned loading into a game of blocks.
senses.whyCN: 统一的尺寸，把装货变成了一场积木游戏。

intro.en: Container is contain plus the thing ending -er, from Latin continere, to hold together.
intro.cn: container 是 contain 加表物的词尾 -er，源自拉丁语 continere（握在一起）。

items.en: Tenere meant to hold, and continere meant to hold together.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住，continere 意为拢在一起。

items.en: The idea named both a space and what it kept.
items.cn: 这一概念同时指空间与空间所盛之物。

items.en: French contenir supplied the verb behind the English noun.
items.cn: 法语 contenir 提供了英语名词背后的动词。

items.en: English container first meant any vessel or holder.
items.cn: 英语 container 最初指任何盛器。

items.en: World trade gave the word its huge steel-box sense.
items.cn: 世界贸易赋予它大型钢制货箱的含义。

items.en: It now means both a kitchen jar and a cargo box.
items.cn: 如今它既指厨房的罐子，也指货运的箱子。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the contain- family, and the meaning group names other things made to hold something.
note.cn: 形近组共享 contain- 词族，近义组列出其他用来盛物的东西。

entries.definition: to have something inside
the act of keeping something under control
the things inside a container
a container for liquid, or a ship
an object used to hold something
a container with stiff sides and a lid

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a jar on a kitchen shelf, then move to a tall stack of steel boxes at a port.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从厨房架上的一只罐子开始，再到港口高高堆起的钢箱。

normal.en: Contain plus -er means the thing that does the holding.
normal.cn: contain 加 -er，就是负责盛住东西的那个物件。

normal.en: A jar, a bottle and a steel box all do the same job at different sizes.
normal.cn: 罐子、瓶子和钢箱只是尺寸不同，干的却是同一件事。

normal.en: Kitchens have containers; ports have containers; the word travels well.
normal.cn: 厨房有容器，港口有集装箱，这个词走得很远。

normal.en: Open the lid and the contents become visible.
normal.cn: 打开盖子，里面的东西才看得见。

normal.en: A container is judged by what it keeps dry.
normal.cn: 一个容器好不好，要看它让什么保持干燥。

abstract.en: Picture a row of coloured steel boxes at a port.
abstract.cn: 想象港口一排彩色的钢箱。

abstract.en: Picture a glass jar with a tight metal lid.
abstract.cn: 想象一只带紧金属盖的玻璃罐。

abstract.en: Picture a crane setting one box on another.
abstract.cn: 想象吊机把一只箱子放到另一只上。

examples.en: She stored the rice in a sealed container.
examples.cn: 她把米存放在密封容器里。

examples.en: The container ship docked before noon.
examples.cn: 那艘集装箱船在正午前靠港。

examples.en: Each container holds about twenty tons.
examples.cn: 每只集装箱能装大约二十吨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 container 记成 contain（容纳）加 er（物）：专门用来容纳东西的物件，就是容器，放大到货运就是集装箱。

root: 由 contain（容纳）加表物词尾 -er 构成，词根为拉丁语 continere（com 一起 + tenere 握住），后指各类容器与货运集装箱。

sensesIntro.en: From the jar that keeps flour dry, to the steel box that crosses an ocean.
sensesIntro.cn: 从让面粉保持干燥的罐子，到跨越大洋的钢箱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of tall steel boxes stacked at a port.
core.cn: 核心意象：港口堆着一排高大的钢箱。

branches.en: The first sense is any small shell for daily things.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是日常物品的任意小外壳。

branches.en: The second sense is that same idea grown to ship size.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是同一想法长到轮船的尺寸。

branches.en: Both senses protect what is inside from the outside.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保护里面不受外面影响。

branches.en: A good lid matters as much as a good box.
branches.cn: 好盖子与好箱子一样重要。

branches.en: One standard size lets ships, trains and trucks share a load.
branches.cn: 一种标准尺寸，让船、火车与卡车共用一批货。

intro.en: Container is contain plus the thing ending -er, from Latin continere, to hold together.
intro.cn: container 是 contain 加表物词尾 -er，源自拉丁语 continere（拢在一起）。

latinIntro.en: The Latin hold base tain- also appears in maintain, obtain and retain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的握持词基 tain- 也出现在 maintain、obtain 与 retain 中。

items.meaning: an object that holds other things
items.example: The container is easy to carry.

items.meaning: the keeping of something within limits
items.example: Containment of the virus took weeks.

items.meaning: to pack goods into standard boxes
items.example: They containerize the fruit for export.

items.meaning: to keep something in good order
to get something into your hands

definition_zh: 笨手笨脚的；粗糙笨重的；不得体的
definition_en: moving or handling things in an awkward way, badly made, or not tactful
core_image: 端着一摞盘子撞上门框时手肘一歪
scene: 他端着一摞盘子，走过窄门时手肘撞到了门框。 He made a clumsy attempt to catch the falling cup.
sceneCN: 这里 clumsy 指「笨手笨脚的」（第 1 个义项：动作不灵巧）；句意是他笨拙地伸手去接掉落的杯子。

pos.zh: 笨手笨脚的；粗糙的；不得体的

senses.title: Awkward in movement
senses.definition: moving the body or handling objects in a way that is not smooth
senses.definitionCN: 身体动作或拿取物件时不灵巧流畅
senses.example: Her clumsy fingers dropped the key twice.
senses.exampleCN: 她笨拙的手指把钥匙掉了两次。
senses.why: The word first described limbs stiff with cold, so awkward movement is its oldest picture.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初形容冻僵的四肢，因此不灵巧的动作是它最古老的画面。

senses.title: Badly made or designed
senses.definition: made or built in a rough way that shows little skill
senses.definitionCN: 制作或建造粗糙，显出缺少手艺
senses.example: The table was a clumsy copy of a French design.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子是对法式设计的粗糙模仿。
senses.why: A hand that cannot work smoothly leaves marks on the things it makes.
senses.whyCN: 不灵巧的手会在它做出的东西上留下痕迹。

senses.title: Not tactful
senses.definition: said or done without skill or care for other people's feelings
senses.definitionCN: 说话做事缺少技巧，未顾及他人感受
senses.example: He made a clumsy apology and left the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他笨拙地道了个歉，然后离开了房间。
senses.why: Words can be handled as badly as objects, so social mistakes borrowed the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 话语和物件一样会被拿得很糟，于是社交失误也用了同一个形容词。

intro.en: Clumsy began with cold-stiffened limbs, not with a lack of skill.
intro.cn: clumsy 最初说的是被冻僵的四肢，而不是缺少技巧。

items.en: Clumsen meant to be numb or stiff with cold.
items.cn: clumsen 指被冻得麻木或僵硬。

items.en: Clumsy described limbs that were stiff with cold.
items.cn: clumsy 形容被冻僵的四肢。

items.en: The sense widened to any awkward movement.
items.cn: 含义扩展到任何不灵巧的动作。

items.en: Clumsy work meant rough work done without skill.
items.cn: clumsy work 指缺少手艺的粗活。

items.en: The word now also covers tactless remarks and awkward timing.
items.cn: 这个词如今还指不得体的话语与尴尬的时机。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in sound or spelling, while the meaning group names awkwardness.
note.cn: 形近组收读音或拼写接近的词，近义组列出笨拙的说法。

entries.definition: unpleasantly damp and sticky
in an awkward and unskilful way
entries.definitionCN: 以笨拙而不熟练的方式

entries.definition: the quality of moving without skill
moving in a way that looks uncomfortable
moving in a heavy and clumsy way
having no skill for a task
entries.definitionCN: 对某项事务毫无技巧的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use cold fingers, the dropped cup and the apology that lands badly.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从冻僵的手指、掉落的杯子和说砸了的道歉入手。

normal.en: Clumsy fingers in winter cannot button a coat, and that is where the word began.
normal.cn: 冬天冻僵的手指扣不上外套，这正是这个词的起点。

normal.en: Clumsy ends in y like many adjectives, and the adverb swaps y for ily.
normal.cn: clumsy 像许多形容词一样以 y 结尾，副词把 y 换成 ily。

normal.en: A clumsy table looks as if a hand shook while cutting it.
normal.cn: clumsy table 看起来像下锯时手在抖。

normal.en: A clumsy apology is a sentence that trips over itself.
normal.cn: clumsy apology 就是一句自己绊倒自己的话。

normal.en: Clumsiness adds -ness and turns the quality into a noun.
normal.cn: clumsiness 加 -ness，把这种特质变成名词。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of plates tipping while a man reaches for the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞盘子倾斜，而那人正伸手去够门。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden chair with one leg a little too short.
abstract.cn: 想象一把木椅，其中一条腿短了一点。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker stopping in the middle of a wrong word.
abstract.cn: 想象一位说话者卡在一个用错的词中间。

examples.en: His clumsy hands knocked over the glass.
examples.cn: 他笨拙的手把玻璃杯碰倒了。

examples.en: The first version of the tool was heavy and clumsy.
examples.cn: 这个工具最初的版本又重又笨。

examples.en: She made a clumsy joke about his new haircut.
examples.cn: 她拿他的新发型开了个不得体的玩笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 clumsy 记成「冻僵的手」：手指不听使唤，做什么都碰倒东西。

root: 源自中古英语 clumsen（冻得麻木僵硬），后由僵硬的肢体引申为动作笨拙。

sensesIntro.en: From stiff cold limbs to rough work and then to words that handle feelings badly.
sensesIntro.cn: 从冻僵的四肢，到粗糙的手工，再到不会照顾感受的话语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands that cannot move smoothly and knock things over.
core.cn: 核心意象：动作不顺畅的手把东西碰倒。

branches.en: The body sense keeps the oldest picture of stiff, cold hands.
branches.cn: 身体义保留了冻僵双手的最古老画面。

branches.en: An unskilful hand leaves its awkwardness in the object.
branches.cn: 不灵巧的手把笨拙留在了物件上。

branches.en: Words can be dropped as easily as cups.
branches.cn: 话语和杯子一样容易掉在地上。

branches.en: Both senses rest on a lack of smooth control.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在缺少顺畅控制之上。

branches.en: Rough making and rough speaking both show a missing skill.
branches.cn: 做活粗糙与说话粗糙都显出技巧的缺失。

intro.en: The stem grows comparison forms, an adverb and a noun, plus a few compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词干长出比较级、副词与名词，并构成若干复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the root is the Middle English verb clumsen, to be numb with cold.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，词根是中古英语动词 clumsen（冻得麻木）。

items.example: His left hand is the clumsier of the two.
items.exampleCN: 他左手比右手更不灵巧。

items.example: That was the clumsiest attempt of the day.
items.exampleCN: 那是当天最笨拙的一次尝试。
他笨手笨脚地折起地图。
clumse 衍生出形容词 clumsy。

items.example: The boy was clumsy-handed with small tools.
items.exampleCN: 这男孩用起小工具来手很笨。

items.example: He was clumsy-footed on the stairs.
The machine is clumsy-looking but strong.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器样子笨拙却很结实。

definition_zh: 怀疑的；拿不准的；不太可能的；可疑的
definition_en: not sure about something, or unlikely to happen or to be true
core_image: 眉头皱起、嘴角下压的那张脸，写满拿不准
scene: 母亲看着窗外越压越低的乌云，对出门的计划犹豫起来。 She looked doubtful when I suggested a picnic.
sceneCN: 这里 doubtful 是「怀疑的、拿不准的」（第 1 个义项）；句意是我提议去野餐时，她露出拿不准的神情。

pos.zh: 形容词：怀疑的；拿不准的；不太可能的；可疑的

derivatives.zh: 由 doubtful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「怀疑地；拿不准地」
由 doubtful 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「可疑；不确定」

senses.title: Feeling unsure about something
senses.definition: not certain whether something is true, right, or a good idea
senses.definitionCN: 不能确定某事是否真实、正确，或是否是个好主意
senses.example: She was doubtful about accepting the offer.
senses.exampleCN: 她对是否接受这个提议拿不准。
senses.why: The -ful suffix turns doubt into a full state, so the person is filled with the wavering of the base word.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ful 把 doubt 变成「充满」的状态，于是人整个被那种摇摆填满，这就是拿不准。

senses.title: Unlikely to happen or be true
senses.definition: not likely to happen, succeed, or be true
senses.definitionCN: 发生的可能性很小，难以成功或不像是真的
senses.example: It is doubtful that the team will finish the bridge this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍今年修完这座桥的可能性不大。
senses.why: When the scale leans clearly toward no, the wavering resolves into a judgement of improbability.
senses.whyCN: 当天平明显偏向「不」这一边时，摇摆就凝固成一句判断：事情不太可能发生。

senses.title: Probably not honest or reliable
senses.definition: likely to be dishonest, unsafe, or of poor quality
senses.definitionCN: 很可能不诚实、不安全，或质量靠不住的
senses.example: The dealer offered a doubtful excuse for the missing papers.
senses.exampleCN: 车商为缺失的文件给出了一个可疑的借口。
senses.why: Once the uncertainty attaches to a person or a thing rather than a fact, the same adjective means shady.
senses.whyCN: 当这种不确定从「事情」转到「人或物」身上，同一个形容词就变成了「来路可疑」。

intro.en: Doubtful is the English word doubt with the adjective suffix -ful, whose older sense was full of.
intro.cn: doubtful 是英语词 doubt 加上形容词后缀 -ful 构成的，后者较早的意思是「充满」。

items.en: Latin dubius described something wavering between two possibilities.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dubius 形容在两种可能之间摇摆的事物。

items.en: The verb dubitare meant to hesitate, and its noun dubium named a doubtful matter.
items.cn: 动词 dubitare 意为「犹豫」，其名词 dubium 指存疑之事。

items.en: French kept the meaning while losing the b in speech and spelling.
items.cn: 法语保留了词义，却在口语与拼写中丢掉了 b。

items.en: English formed doute from the French verb and used it for both the feeling and the verb.
items.cn: 中古英语由法语动词造出 doute，名词与动词两种用法并存。

items.en: The suffix -ful was added to make an adjective; the earliest examples are dated only approximately.
items.cn: 加上 -ful 构成形容词，最早用例只能大致定在十四世纪。

items.en: The b returned in spelling, and doubtful spread from people to outcomes and to suspicious things.
items.cn: b 在拼写上回归，doubtful 也从形容人扩展到形容结果与可疑之物。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same stem; the near-meaning group separates three shades of not being sure.
note.cn: 形近组都建在同一个词干上；近义组区分三种「拿不准」的程度。

entries.definition: To feel unsure, or the feeling of uncertainty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「怀疑；疑问」，是 doubtful 的基础词。

entries.definition: Certainly; without any doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「无疑地」，与 doubtful 同族但意思相反。

entries.definition: Doubtful or suspicious; closer to the Latin original.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「怀疑的；可疑的」，比 doubtful 更贴近拉丁原形。

entries.definition: Not known or not decided; it can describe facts as well as people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不确定的」，既可形容人也可形容情况，范围比 doubtful 宽。

entries.definition: Doubting claims that others accept, often after careful thought.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「持怀疑态度的」，多指经过思考后不接受他人说法。

entries.definition: Not probable; it states probability only and says nothing about feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不太可能的」，只谈概率，不含主观情绪。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work through the -ful suffix and the two directions the base word can lean.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子围绕 -ful 后缀，以及基础词可能倒向的两个方向展开。

normal.en: Doubt plus -ful means full of doubt, exactly like careful means full of care.
normal.cn: doubt 加 -ful 就是「充满怀疑」，和 careful 表示「充满小心」是一个道理。

normal.en: A doubtful person is not empty of answers but crowded with questions.
normal.cn: doubtful 的人不是没有答案，而是被问题挤满了。

normal.en: When the scale leans to no, doubtful means unlikely, not just unsure.
normal.cn: 当天平倒向「不」，doubtful 就表示「不太可能」，而不只是「拿不准」。

normal.en: Applied to things rather than facts, the same word means suspicious.
normal.cn: 把它用在物品而不是事实身上，同一个词就表示「可疑」。

normal.en: Doubtless is its opposite twin, made with -less instead of -ful.
normal.cn: doubtless 是它的反义双胞胎，只是把 -ful 换成了 -less。

abstract.en: Picture a face with one eyebrow lifted and the mouth pulled sideways.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸，一边眉毛挑起，嘴角向旁边撇。

abstract.en: Picture a weather vane spinning between two winds.
abstract.cn: 想象风向标在两股风之间来回打转。

abstract.en: Picture a folder marked with a large question mark instead of a title.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件夹，标题的位置画着一个大问号。

examples.en: The doctor was doubtful about the test results.
examples.cn: 医生对检查结果持怀疑态度。

examples.en: It seems doubtful that the shop will reopen this month.
examples.cn: 这家店这个月重新开张的可能性似乎不大。

examples.en: They bought the car from a doubtful dealer.
examples.cn: 他们从一个可疑的车商那里买了这辆车。

dict_mnemonic.text: doubt 是「怀疑」，-ful 是「充满」，合起来就是「满肚子怀疑」；再一转，就成「不太可能」和「可疑」。

root: 由 doubt 加形容词后缀 -ful（充满……的）构成。doubt 经古法语来自拉丁语 dubitare（摇摆、犹豫），源头 dubius（在两者间摇摆）。-ful 在古英语中本义就是「充满」，因此 doubtful 字面意思是「充满怀疑的」。

sensesIntro.en: The suffix turns wavering into a filled state, which then splits into unsure, improbable and suspicious.
sensesIntro.cn: 后缀把摇摆变成一种被填满的状态，这个状态再分成「拿不准」「不太可能」「可疑」三路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face wrinkled by a scale that will not settle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被「不肯落定的秤」拧出纹路的脸。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the filled state first describes someone who cannot decide.
branches.cn: 人物线：被填满的状态先形容一个下不了决心的人，即第一个义项。

branches.en: THE OUTCOME: when the scale leans to no, the adjective judges an event improbable.
branches.cn: 结果线：当天平倒向「不」，这个形容词就判断某事不太可能，即第二个义项。

branches.en: THE THING: attached to an object or a story, the same word means shady.
branches.cn: 物品线：把它安到某件东西或某套说法上，同一个词就表示可疑，即第三个义项。

branches.en: A doubtful person and a doubtful excuse share the same refusal to stand firm.
branches.cn: 拿不准的人与可疑的借口，共享同一种「站不稳」的性质。

branches.en: An unlikely plan and a suspicious offer both invite caution before action.
branches.cn: 不太可能的计划与可疑的提议，都提醒人在行动前先留个心眼。

intro.en: Doubtful is a transparent English build: a borrowed stem plus a native suffix.
intro.cn: doubtful 是结构透明的英语构词：一个借来的词干加一个本土后缀。

latinIntro.en: The stem comes from Latin dubius and dubitare; -ful is a native English suffix meaning full of.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自拉丁语 dubius 与 dubitare；-ful 是英语本土后缀，意为「充满」。

items.example: The Latin adjective is the ultimate source of the stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词是词干的最初来源。

items.example: The verb gave French its word for doubting.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「怀疑」传给了法语。

items.example: Doubt is the base of doubtful.
items.exampleCN: doubt 是 doubtful 的基础词。
它把 doubt 变成 doubtful。

items.example: It forms undoubtful in older texts.
items.exampleCN: 在较早文本中它构成 undoubtful。

derivatives.zh: 由 doubtful 加 -ly 构成，义为「怀疑地」
由 doubtful 加 -ness 构成，义为「可疑；不确定」

definition_zh: 给…穿衣；为…提供衣物；用言语表达
definition_en: to put clothes on someone, to provide clothes for people, or to express an idea in words
core_image: 母亲把厚外套披到孩子肩上
scene: 冬天出发前，母亲把厚外套一件件披到孩子身上。 Volunteers clothe the children before the cold season.
sceneCN: 这里 clothe 指「为…提供衣物」（第 2 个义项：给人们提供衣服）；句意是志愿者在寒季到来前为孩子们提供衣物。

pos.zh: 给…穿衣；为…提供衣物；表达

senses.title: Put clothes on someone
senses.definition: to dress someone in clothes
senses.definitionCN: 给某人穿上衣服
senses.example: She clothed the baby in a wool jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 她给宝宝穿上一件毛外套。
senses.why: The verb was built directly from the old noun for cloth, so it names the act of covering a body.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词直接由表示布的古名词构成，因此指给身体覆上衣物。

senses.title: Provide clothes for people
senses.definition: to supply clothes to a group of people who need them
senses.definitionCN: 向需要衣服的一群人提供衣物
senses.example: The charity clothes three hundred families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构为三百个家庭提供衣物。
senses.why: Helping others dress extends the single act into regular support.
senses.whyCN: 帮助他人穿衣把这个单一动作扩展为长期帮扶。

senses.title: Express in words
senses.definition: to cover an idea with words, as if dressing it
senses.definitionCN: 像给想法穿上衣服一样用词语把它包起来
senses.example: He clothed his anger in polite words.
senses.exampleCN: 他用客气话把怒气包了起来。
senses.why: An idea without words looks naked, so dressing it became a metaphor for expressing it.
senses.whyCN: 没有词语的想法像是赤裸的，给它穿衣便成了表达的比喻。

intro.en: Clothe is the old verb built from cloth, and it has always meant covering a body.
intro.cn: clothe 是由 cloth 构成的古老动词，一直表示给身体覆上衣物。

items.en: Claþian meant to put clothes on someone.
items.cn: claþian 指给某人穿上衣服。

items.en: The verb kept the same stem as the noun for cloth.
items.cn: 这个动词与表示布的名词共用词干。

items.en: Clothe gained the figurative sense of covering an idea.
items.cn: clothe 获得了包裹想法的比喻义。

items.en: Clothing became the usual noun for garments.
items.cn: clothing 成为衣物的常用名词。

items.en: The verb now also means to supply clothes to people in need.
items.cn: 这个动词如今还指向有需要的人提供衣物。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the cloth family, while the meaning group names the act of dressing.
note.cn: 形近组收 cloth 家族，近义组列出穿衣的动作。

entries.definition: woven material used for clothes or cleaning
entries.definitionCN: 用来做衣或擦拭的织物

entries.definition: the things people wear on their bodies
dressed in a particular way
to put clothes on yourself or another person
entries.definitionCN: 给自己或他人穿上衣服

entries.definition: to dress someone in fine or special clothes
entries.definitionCN: 给某人穿上讲究或特别的衣服

entries.definition: to dress someone in a stated kind of clothing
entries.definitionCN: 给某人穿上某种特定的服装

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cloth inside the word and the picture of dressing a child.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从词里的 cloth 和给孩子穿衣的画面入手。

normal.en: Clothe is cloth plus a verb ending: give someone the cloth to wear.
normal.cn: clothe 就是 cloth 加动词词尾：把布给人穿上。

normal.en: Cloth and clothe differ by one letter and one sound.
normal.cn: cloth 与 clothe 只差一个字母和一个音。

normal.en: The past form clothed keeps the full stem, unlike dressed or clad.
normal.cn: 过去式 clothed 保留完整词干，与 dressed 或 clad 不同。

normal.en: To clothe an idea is to give it words as a coat.
normal.cn: 给想法穿衣，就是给它套上词语的外套。

normal.en: Clothing is the noun that names what the verb puts on.
normal.cn: clothing 正是这个动词所穿上之物的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a mother bending to button a small coat.
abstract.cn: 想象一位母亲弯腰给小孩扣外套。

abstract.en: Picture boxes of coats handed out on a cold morning.
abstract.cn: 想象寒冷的早晨，一箱箱外套被递出去。

abstract.en: Picture a rough idea wrapped in neat sentences.
abstract.cn: 想象一个粗糙的想法被整齐的句子包起来。

examples.en: The nurse clothed the patient in a clean gown.
examples.cn: 护士给病人换上干净的病号服。

examples.en: The charity clothes and feeds the families each winter.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构每年冬天为这些家庭提供衣食。

examples.en: He clothed the plain fact in gentle language.
examples.cn: 他用温和的措辞把这一事实包了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 clothe 记成「把布披上」：布里藏着 cloth，动作就是给人穿衣。

root: 源自古英语 claþian（给…穿衣），由名词 claþ（布；衣服）派生的动词。

sensesIntro.en: From dressing one body to supplying clothes for many, then to dressing an idea in words.
sensesIntro.cn: 从给一个人穿衣，到为许多人供衣，再到给想法披上词语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat settled over a child's shoulders.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件外套落在孩子肩上。

branches.en: The basic act is covering one body with clothes.
branches.cn: 基本动作是给一具身体穿上衣物。

branches.en: The same act repeated for many people becomes supply.
branches.cn: 同一动作对许多人重复，就成了供给。

branches.en: Words work as clothes for an idea that would otherwise stand bare.
branches.cn: 词语就是想法本会赤裸时穿的衣物。

branches.en: One person dressed and a group dressed share the verb.
branches.cn: 给一个人穿衣与给一群人穿衣共用一个动词。

branches.en: Both senses are about covering what needs protection.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是给需要保护的东西加覆盖。

intro.en: The stem folds into compounds and participles, all tied to clothing.
intro.cn: 这个词干融入复合词与分词，都与衣物相关。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the root is the Old English noun claþ.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，词根是古英语名词 claþ。

items.example: She clothes the children before school.
items.exampleCN: 她送孩子上学前给他们穿衣。

items.example: The hills were clothed in mist.
Warm clothing is the first need.
The workers were clad in blue.
The statue shows an unclothed figure.
items.exampleCN: 这尊雕像呈现一个裸身人像。

items.example: She hung the sheets on the clothesline.
items.exampleCN: 她把床单挂到晾衣绳上。

items.example: The clotheshorse stood by the window.
He works in a small clothes shop.
items.exampleCN: 他在一家小服装店工作。

definition_zh: 歌剧；歌剧艺术；歌剧院；歌剧团
definition_en: a dramatic work set to music and sung by trained singers, usually with an orchestra, and also the art form or the house where it is staged
core_image: 歌唱者站在彩绘布景前，乐队在乐池里等最后一个音符落下
scene: 假期最后一晚，一家人换上正式衣服，走进河边那座老剧场，准备从头听到尾。 The whole family dressed up to hear an opera that lasted four hours.
sceneCN: 这里是「歌剧作品」（第 1 个义项：谱成音乐、由歌手演唱的戏剧）；句意为一家人盛装去听一部长达四小时的歌剧。图中可辨识物件：舞台布景、乐池、观众席。

pos.zh: 歌剧；歌剧艺术；歌剧院；歌剧团

derivatives.zh: 由 opera 加 -ic 构成，义为「歌剧的；歌剧式的」
意大利语 operetta 是 opera 的指小形式，义为「轻歌剧」
直接来自拉丁语 opus（作品），与 opera 同出一源，义为「作品；乐曲」

senses.title: A drama sung on stage
senses.definition: a play set to music, in which the story is told through singing rather than ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 谱成音乐的戏剧，故事用歌唱而不是日常说话来讲
senses.example: The new opera was written by a young composer.
senses.exampleCN: 这部新歌剧由一位年轻作曲家写成。
senses.why: Latin opera is the plural of opus, a work; Italian took it for a musical work, and English borrowed that name for the kind of drama that is sung.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 opera 是 opus（作品）的复数；意大利语借它指「谱成音乐的作品」，英语再借来，就成了这类唱着演的戏剧的名字。

senses.title: The art form itself
senses.titleCN: 歌剧艺术；歌剧这一体裁
senses.definition: the art form or genre of such works, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把这类作品作为整体来看的艺术形式或门类
senses.example: She has spent thirty years in opera.
senses.exampleCN: 她在歌剧这一行干了三十年。
senses.why: Once it names individual works, the word can name the whole field those works belong to, just as a kind of object can give its name to a craft.
senses.whyCN: 既然能指一部部作品，也就能指这些作品所属的整个领域；就像某类物件可以给出一个行当的名字。

senses.title: The building or the company
senses.definition: the theatre, or the company, where such works are staged
senses.definitionCN: 上演这类作品的剧院，或经营它的团体
senses.example: The opera is rebuilding its stage this winter.
senses.exampleCN: 歌剧院今年冬天要重修它的舞台。
senses.why: A place or an institution often takes the name of the art it presents, so the word moves from the work to the house that performs it.
senses.whyCN: 演出场所或团体常直接拿它所演的艺术来命名，词义就从「作品」转到「上演作品的房子」。

intro.en: Opera reached English through Italian, but behind it sits the Latin word for a work; its family includes opus and operatic, not the separate verb for working.
intro.cn: opera 经意大利语进入英语，背后却是拉丁语中「作品」这个词；同族词包括 opus 与 operatic，而不包括另一个表示「干活」的动词。

items.en: Latin opus meant work, effort or a product, and its plural opera meant works; the genitive operis keeps the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语 opus 指工作、出力或成果，复数 opera 指多件作品；属格 operis 保留同一词干。

items.en: In Latin, opera could already name a work of art, and the phrase opera in musica named a work set to music.
items.cn: 在拉丁语中 opera 已经可以指一件艺术品，短语 opera in musica 专指「谱成音乐的作品」。

items.en: Italian composers and audiences made opera the name of the new sung drama, and that sense became fixed.
items.cn: 十七世纪的意大利作曲家与观众拿 opera 当作这种新的歌唱戏剧的名字，词义就此固定下来。

items.en: English borrowed the Italian word and soon used it for the building where such works were staged, giving opera house.
items.cn: 英语借入这个意大利词，很快又用它指上演这类作品的建筑，于是有了 opera house。

items.en: Modern English keeps the musical sense and loosens it in soap opera, where the link is serial drama rather than song.
items.cn: 现代英语保留音乐戏剧的含义，并在 soap opera 里把这种联系放宽到长篇连续剧，与歌唱无关。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin words for a work and the operatic family; the near-meaning group gathers other staged or sung arts.
note.cn: 形近组收与「作品」有关、来自拉丁语的同族词；近义组收其他舞台或声乐艺术。

entries.definition: Relating to opera, or exaggerated in the manner of opera.
entries.definitionCN: 与歌剧有关的，或像歌剧那样夸张的。

entries.definition: A work of art, especially a musical composition.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术作品，尤指音乐作品。

entries.definition: A short, light opera with spoken dialogue and songs.
entries.definitionCN: 有对白与唱段的短小轻歌剧。

entries.definition: A comic opera in the Italian tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利传统中的喜歌剧。

entries.definition: A stage show that mixes songs, dance and spoken scenes.
entries.definitionCN: 把歌曲、舞蹈与对白场面混合的舞台演出。

entries.definition: A long musical work on a sacred subject, sung without staging.
entries.definitionCN: 以宗教题材写成、只唱不演的长篇音乐作品。

entries.definition: A staged dance work with music but without singing.
entries.definitionCN: 有音乐、无歌唱的舞台舞蹈作品。

normalIntro.en: Opera is a Latin plural that Italian turned into the name of a sung play, and the family keeps circling the idea of a work.
normalIntro.cn: opera 本是拉丁语的复数形式，意大利语把它变成一路唱着演的戏剧之名；这一族词都绕着「作品」打转。

normal.en: Opera is the plural of opus, so the word literally means works.
normal.cn: opera 是 opus 的复数，字面上就是「多件作品」。

normal.en: The Latin phrase opera in musica is the seed of the modern sense: a work set to music.
normal.cn: 拉丁短语 opera in musica 是现代词义的种子：谱上音乐的「作品」。

normal.en: Opera house names the building after the art, a common pattern for theatres.
normal.cn: opera house 用艺术之名来命名建筑，这是剧院常见的命名方式。

normal.en: Operatic adds -ic, meaning belonging to opera or behaving like someone on its stage.
normal.cn: operatic 加 -ic，意为属于歌剧的，或像站在歌剧舞台上那样夸张。

normal.en: Operetta is a small opera, because the Italian diminutive makes the genre light and short.
normal.cn: operetta 是「小歌剧」，意大利语的指小形式让这个门类变得轻巧短小。

abstract.en: One word for works, a genre and a building shows how a single name can shelter a whole art.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指作品、门类和建筑，说明一个名字可以把一门艺术整个罩住。

abstract.en: The audience sits in the dark while a story is carried entirely by the human voice.
abstract.cn: 观众坐进黑暗里，整个故事只靠人声扛着走。

abstract.en: Singing turns ordinary speech into something too large for a living room.
abstract.cn: 歌唱把日常说话放大成客厅装不下的东西。

examples.en: The new opera was written by a young composer.
examples.cn: 这部新歌剧由一位年轻作曲家写成。

examples.en: She has spent thirty years in opera.
examples.cn: 她在歌剧这一行干了三十年。

examples.en: The opera is rebuilding its stage this winter.
examples.cn: 歌剧院今年冬天要重修它的舞台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，泼啦」——台上唱得太投入，茶水泼了满地也不管；记住 opera 是歌剧。

root: 拉丁语 opus（工作、成果，属格 operis）的复数 opera 意为「作品」，意大利语用它指「谱成音乐的戏剧」，十七世纪传入英语。它与 operate 不是同一个词：operate 来自拉丁动词 operari（干活、起作用），两条路线不同，现代英语里不能互换。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a work set to music; the senses divide into one staged work, the art form as a whole, and the house or company that presents it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「谱成音乐的成品」；义项分为一部具体的舞台作品、作为整体的艺术门类，以及上演它的场所或团体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a singer standing before a painted set while the orchestra waits in the pit.
core.cn: 核心意象：歌唱者站在彩绘布景前，乐队在乐池里等最后一个音符。

branches.en: a young composer finishing a score late at night
branches.cn: 年轻作曲家深夜写完一部总谱

branches.en: the curtain falling after the last aria
branches.cn: 最后一段咏叹调唱完，幕布落下

branches.en: a singer choosing a life on the stage
branches.cn: 歌唱者选择以舞台为业

branches.en: a stone theatre lit up on opening night
branches.cn: 首演之夜灯火通明的石砌剧院

branches.en: a company loading scenery onto a truck for a tour
branches.cn: 剧团把布景装上卡车去巡演

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin plural for works, passes through Italian, and gathers English compounds for the house, the singer and the company.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「作品」的复数形式上，经意大利语中转，再在英语里聚起一批指剧院、演员和剧团的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family behind opera is the opus family: a work, its plural, and the adjectives built on them.
latinIntro.cn: opera 背后的拉丁词族是 opus 一族：作品、它的复数，以及由它们构成的形容词。

items.meaning: plural marker of the first declension

definition_zh: 很可能的；可信的；有理由的；有相当根据的
definition_en: likely to happen or to be true, or reasonable enough to be believed
core_image: 天平两端各放一份证据，装证据较多的一侧缓缓下沉
scene: 气象员指着西边压来的云层，判断傍晚前会有雷暴。 A storm is probable by evening.
