sceneCN: 这里指「很可能会发生的」（第 1 个义项：事件很可能发生）；句意为傍晚之前很可能有一场雷暴。可辨识物件：云层、风向标、雷达图、记录板；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 很可能的；可信的；有理由的

senses.title: Likely to happen
senses.definition: having a strong chance of happening
senses.definitionCN: 发生的可能性很大
senses.example: A storm is probable by evening.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚之前很可能有一场雷暴。
senses.why: The Latin adjective means 'that can be approved', and what can be approved is what the evidence supports.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词意为「可获认可的」，而可获认可的就是证据所支持的东西。

senses.title: Credible as an account
senses.definition: likely to be true, said of a story or an explanation
senses.definitionCN: 很可能为真，用于说法或解释
senses.example: Her version of events is probable, though not proved.
senses.exampleCN: 她对事情的描述很可信，尽管未获证明。
senses.why: The oldest sense concerns belief rather than events: a probable account is one worthy of acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项关乎相信而非事件：可信的说法就是值得接受的说法。

senses.title: Supported by reasoning
senses.definition: resting on reasons that make it sensible to accept
senses.definitionCN: 有理由支撑，使接受它显得合理
senses.example: The simplest probable explanation is often the right one.
senses.exampleCN: 最简单的、说得通的解释往往就是对的。
senses.why: A conclusion is probable when the reasons for it outweigh the reasons against, a weighing rather than a proof.
senses.whyCN: 当支持的理由重于反对的理由，结论就是「说得通」的；这是称量，而非证明。

senses.title: Reasonable grounds in law
senses.definition: having enough evidence for an officer to act, in the fixed phrase probable cause
senses.definitionCN: 证据足以让执法人员采取行动，用于固定说法「合理根据」
senses.example: The search was allowed because there was probable cause.
senses.exampleCN: 由于存在合理根据，这次搜查获得准许。
senses.why: Law borrows the weighing image and asks whether the evidence is strong enough to justify action, not to convict.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用了称量的形象，问的是证据是否足以支持行动，而不是足以定罪。

senses.title: Likely in a scientific estimate
senses.titleCN: 科学估计中的或然结论
senses.definition: likely according to a model or an estimate rather than a certainty
senses.definitionCN: 依模型或估计而言很可能，而非确定
senses.example: The probable range of the signal was published with the data.
senses.exampleCN: 信号的或然范围随数据一并发表。
senses.why: Science states results as probable ranges, keeping the word's sense of what the evidence supports.
senses.whyCN: 科学把结果说成或然范围，保留了「证据所支持」的意思。

senses.title: The expected winner
senses.definition: the competitor expected to win, in the phrase the probable winner
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法中指被预期会赢的参赛者
senses.example: She was the probable winner before the final heat.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后一轮预赛之前，她是最被看好的人。
senses.why: Expectation based on evidence is the same weighing applied to a field of competitors.
senses.whyCN: 基于证据的预期，就是同一种称量用在参赛者身上。

senses.title: A probable opinion in moral theology
senses.definition: an opinion with solid support that may be followed without certainty, in the older theological use
senses.definitionCN: 有可靠依据、无需确定即可采纳的意见，属较早的神学用法
senses.example: The older manuals asked whether a probable opinion could safely be followed.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的手册会问：一个可采意见是否能被安全遵循。
senses.why: This technical sense keeps the Latin meaning exactly: an opinion that can be approved, even without proof.
senses.whyCN: 这个专门义精确保留拉丁原义：一种即使未获证明也可获认可的意见。

senses.title: Belief made reasonable by evidence
senses.titleCN: 抽象：证据使相信成为合理
senses.definition: the quality of a claim whose evidence makes belief reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 一种主张因证据而使相信显得合理的性质
senses.example: What makes the claim probable is not certainty but the weight of the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 使这个主张可信的不是确定性，而是证据的分量。
senses.why: The abstract sense isolates the weighing itself, without naming an event, an account or a court.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把称量本身单独提出来，不指事件、说法或法庭。

intro.en: Probable comes through Old French from Latin probabilis 'that can be approved or proved', an adjective from probare 'to test, prove'. It entered English in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: probable 经古法语来自拉丁形容词 probabilis「可认可、可证明的」，出自动词 probare「检验、证明」；十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: Probare meant 'to test, examine, prove'. It belongs with probus 'good, upright' to an old root of testing and approval; that root is reconstructed.
items.cn: probare 意为「检验、审查、证明」。它与 probus「好、正直」同属一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根属重构形式。

items.en: Probabilis meant 'that can be approved, credible'. It described opinions and evidence long before it described events.
items.cn: probabilis 意为「可获认可的、可信的」，在用于事件之前，长期用于意见与证据。

items.en: Old French probable passed the adjective into English in the fourteenth century, where it first meant credible rather than likely to happen.
items.cn: 古法语 probable 在十四世纪把这个形容词带入英语，最初意为「可信」，而非「很可能发生」。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word was increasingly used of future events, so likelihood joined credibility.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词越来越多用于未来事件，于是「可能发生」与「可信」合并。

items.en: The legal phrase probable cause is a fixed term of art, and its earliest uses are dated only approximately.
items.cn: 法律短语「合理根据」是一个固定术语，其最早用例只能给出约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same proving root that are easily confused; group two holds words for what is likely or believable.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「证明」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示「很可能」或「可信」的词。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for likelihood or credibility; the adjective is its descriptive form.
entries.definitionCN: 表示可能性或可信的抽象名词；形容词是它的描述形式。

entries.definition: Able to be demonstrated; it comes from prove, which shares the Latin proving root but stresses demonstration.
entries.definitionCN: 可被证明的；出自 prove，同享拉丁「证明」词根，但强调实证。

entries.definition: Tending to prove something, used of evidence in law.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于证明某事的，用于法律上的证据。

entries.definition: From plaudere 'to applaud': originally 'deserving applause', hence seemingly reasonable; it is not the proving root.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 plaudere「鼓掌」，原意「值得鼓掌」，引申为「看似有理」；与「证明」词根无关。

entries.definition: The everyday adjective for a strong chance, without the evidential weight that probable carries.
entries.definitionCN: 表示机会很大的日常形容词，不带 probable 那种证据分量。

entries.definition: From credere 'to believe': able to be believed, close to the older sense of probable.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 credere「相信」，意为「可被相信」，接近 probable 较古的义项。

entries.definition: Able to be accepted as true, often said of stories and excuses.
entries.definitionCN: 能被当作真实接受的，常用于说法与借口。

entries.definition: Anticipated as likely to occur, with less emphasis on evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 预期会发生，对证据的强调较少。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'test and approve', so probable first meant believable and only later meant likely to happen.
normal.cn: 词根意为「检验与认可」，因此 probable 先指可信，后来才指很可能发生。

normal.en: One family runs probable, probably, probability, probabilistic, improbable and probity.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：很可能的、很可能、概率、概率的、不太可能的、正直。

normal.en: The legal phrase probable cause is a fixed term, not a free combination.
normal.cn: 法律短语「合理根据」是固定术语，不是可以随意组合的说法。

normal.en: Other words about proof are close relatives: prove, proof, provable, probative.
normal.cn: 其他关于证明的词是近亲：证明、证据、可证明的、有证明力的。

normal.en: Plausible looks like a relative but comes from applause, not from proof.
normal.cn: plausible 看似同族，实际出自「鼓掌」，与「证明」无关。

abstract.en: Picture two pans of evidence on a balance, the heavier one slowly winning.
abstract.cn: 想象天平两端各放一份证据，较重的一侧缓缓占上风。

abstract.en: Picture a witness whose story holds together under every question.
abstract.cn: 想象一位证人的说法在每一次追问下都站得住。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where the standard is enough evidence to act, not enough to convict.
abstract.cn: 想象一个法庭，标准是「足以行动的证据」，而非「足以定罪」。

examples.en: It is probable that the flight will be delayed.
examples.cn: 这趟航班很可能会延误。

examples.en: The police must show probable cause before a search.
examples.cn: 警方在搜查之前必须说明合理根据。

examples.en: The theory is probable but not yet proved.
examples.cn: 这个理论说得通，但尚未获得证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「检验、证明」，加形容词词尾表示「能被……的」：能被检验通过的，先是「可信」，后是「很可能」。

root: 拉丁 probabilis「可认可的」＝ probare「检验、证明」＋形容词词尾 -abilis，与 probus「正直」同属一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根属重构形式。英语十四世纪经古法语传入，最初意为「可信」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: evidence is weighed. When the heavier side carries belief, a statement is credible; when it carries expectation, an event is likely; law and science fix the threshold of action and of conclusion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把证据放到天平上称。较重的一侧支撑相信时，说法就可信；支撑预期时，事件就很可能；法律与科学则各自定出行动与结论的门槛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pans of evidence on a balance, the heavier one slowly winning.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两端各放着一份证据，较重的一侧缓缓占上风。

branches.en: WEIGH: likelihood and credibility are the same balance read toward the future or the past.
branches.cn: 称量：可能发生与可信，是天平朝未来或朝过去读的两个方向。

branches.en: REASON ENOUGH: when reasons outweigh counter-reasons, the conclusion is probable.
branches.cn: 理由足够：当支持的理由重于反对的理由，结论就是说得通的。

branches.en: THE BAR: the law asks only whether there is enough for action.
branches.cn: 门槛：法律只问证据是否足以行动。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE: science and older moral theology both fix what may be held without certainty.
branches.cn: 专门领域：科学与较早的道德神学都定出「无确定也可持有」的范围。

branches.en: EXPECTATION: evidence can also pick a likely winner, or simply make belief reasonable.
branches.cn: 预期：证据也能挑出被看好的人，或只是使相信显得合理。

intro.en: Probable is a Latin adjective from a verb of proving; the same root builds nouns of likelihood and the plain words for proof.
intro.cn: probable 是一个拉丁形容词，出自表示证明的动词；同一词根还构成表示可能性的名词与表示证据的普通词。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare and probus give probabilis, probabilitas and the English family probable, probability, prove and proof.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 probare 与 probus 衍生 probabilis、probabilitas，并给出英语词族 probable、probability、prove、proof。

items.example: The root supplies testing before acceptance.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「先检验再接受」的意思。

items.example: The adjective adds moral approval to the same stock.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给同一词源加上道德认可。

items.example: The adjective names what passes the test.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指能通过检验的东西。

definition_zh: 猛烈地；暴力地；剧烈地
definition_en: in a way that uses great force, or that involves hurting people
core_image: 一扇窗在风里剧烈撞动，玻璃嗡嗡作响
scene: 夜里起了风，旧窗框被吹得来回撞动，玻璃嗡嗡直响，她只好起身去关。 The shutters banged violently against the wall all night.
sceneCN: 这里 violently 是「猛烈地」（第 1 个义项：以极大的力量进行）；句意为百叶窗整夜猛烈地拍打墙面。风里撞动的窗与嗡嗡的玻璃正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -ly 构成的形容词，义为「暴力的；猛烈的」
加前缀 non- 构成，义为「非暴力地」

senses.title: With great physical force
senses.definition: with a very strong physical movement or impact
senses.definitionCN: 以极强的人体动作或冲击力
senses.example: The shutters banged violently against the wall all night.
senses.exampleCN: 百叶窗整夜猛烈地拍打墙面。
senses.why: The adverb answers how a thing moves, and here the answer is with everything it has.
senses.whyCN: 副词回答「怎么动」，这里的回答是「用尽全身之力」。

senses.title: In a way that hurts people
senses.definition: in a manner that involves attacking or harming someone
senses.definitionCN: 以攻击或伤害他人的方式进行
senses.example: The crowd was violently broken up by police.
senses.exampleCN: 人群被警察以暴力方式驱散。
senses.why: The adjective means force against people; the adverb says that the action was done that way.
senses.whyCN: 形容词指针对人的力量；副词说明这一动作正是那样完成的。

senses.title: Extremely, in a sudden and ungoverned way
senses.definition: to an extreme and sudden degree, of changes or reactions
senses.definitionCN: 指变化或反应极端而突然
senses.example: He reacted violently to the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这种药反应剧烈。
senses.why: A body or a system can lurch as if struck, and the adverb marks the lurch.
senses.whyCN: 身体或系统可能像被击中般剧变，副词标记的正是这次剧变。

senses.title: With strong opposition in speech
senses.definition: in a very strong and hostile manner of speaking or objecting
senses.definitionCN: 以非常强烈且对立的言辞表示
senses.example: The plan was violently opposed in the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会上这个计划遭到激烈反对。
senses.why: Words can be thrown as hard as stones, so the adverb slips into argument.
senses.whyCN: 话可以像石头一样掷出，副词于是进入了争论的场景。

senses.title: Of colour or emotion, very intensely
senses.definition: in an intensity that strikes the senses or the feelings hard
senses.definitionCN: 指以冲击感官或情感的方式表现出来
senses.example: The sky was violently red at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落时天空红得刺眼。
senses.why: Anything that hits the eye or heart too hard takes this adverb of force.
senses.whyCN: 凡是过猛地冲击眼睛或心的东西，都用这个表示力量的副词。

intro.en: Violently is the adjective violent plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: violently 是形容词 violent 加副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: Vis meant force, and violentus described what is full of it.
items.cn: vis 意为力量，violentus 形容充满力量之物。

items.en: French violent brought the adjective into English.
items.cn: 法语 violent 把形容词带入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ly turned adjectives into adverbs ruling verbs.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变为修饰动词的副词。

items.en: Violently settled into the adverb of storms, blows, and reactions.
items.cn: violently 固定为风暴、打击与反应的副词。

items.en: It extends to speech and colour, wherever intensity is extreme.
items.cn: 它延伸到言辞与色彩，凡强度极端之处皆可用。

note.en: The first group holds the violent family, the second the adverbs of force and calm.
note.cn: 第一组是 violent 词族，第二组是力量与平静的副词。

entries.definition: using great force
the use of force
without force
in a violet manner
with savage intensity
with rage
suddenly and abruptly
with care and lightness

normalIntro.en: Take the adjective, add -ly, and the manner becomes an adverb of force.
normalIntro.cn: 形容词加 -ly，方式便成了表示力量的副词。

normal.en: Violent plus -ly gives violently, with nothing dropped.
normal.cn: violent 加 -ly 即 violently，中间不省字母。

normal.en: Shake violently is a common pairing in reports.
normal.cn: 新闻报道里 shake violently 常连用。

normal.en: It ends in -ly, but does not mean like a violent person only.
normal.cn: 它虽以 -ly 结尾，却不只表示「像暴徒那样」。

normal.en: Use more violently for comparison.
normal.cn: 比较时用 more violently。

normal.en: The four syllables are light in the middle: VI-o-lent-ly.
normal.cn: 四个音节，中间轻读：VI-o-lent-ly。

abstract.en: See a shutter hammering the wall in a gale.
abstract.cn: 想大风里百叶窗不停拍墙。

abstract.en: Feel an engine judder under a hand.
abstract.cn: 感受手下发动机的抖动。

abstract.en: Picture a red sky that is hard to look at.
abstract.cn: 想一片红得让人不能直视的天空。

examples.en: The plane shook violently as it passed the storm.
examples.cn: 飞机穿越大风区时剧烈颠簸。

examples.en: She was violently sick after the boat trip.
examples.cn: 坐完船她吐得很厉害。

examples.en: The proposal was violently attacked by two members.
examples.cn: 这项提议遭到两位委员的激烈抨击。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪了伦特」——招牌被风吹歪了，伦特家的大门被拍得咣咣响。

root: 拉丁语 vis（力量）→ violentus → 古法语 violent → 英语 violent + -ly → violently

sensesIntro.en: How things move, strike, react, argue, and glow: one adverb answers all of them with force.
sensesIntro.cn: 东西怎么动、怎么撞、怎么反应、怎么争论、怎么发光：一个副词一律答以「猛烈」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window slamming in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：风中来回撞击的窗。

branches.en: The shutter branch: banging against the wall.
branches.cn: 百叶窗分支：不停拍墙。

branches.en: The crowd branch: police breaking it up by force.
branches.cn: 人群分支：警察以暴力驱散。

branches.en: The medicine branch: the body lurching in reaction.
branches.cn: 药物分支：身体的剧烈反应。

branches.en: The meeting branch: a plan opposed with heat.
branches.cn: 会议分支：计划遭激烈反对。

branches.en: The sunset branch: a sky too red to bear.
branches.cn: 落日分支：红得刺眼的天空。

intro.en: The stem viol- means force; -ent and -ly turn it first into an adjective, then an adverb.
intro.cn: 词干 viol- 意为力量，-ent 与 -ly 依次把它变为形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vis, force, gives violentus; English adds -ly to make the manner adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vis（力量）派生 violentus，英语再加 -ly 构成方式副词。

items.example: Viol- is the force in the word.
Violently tells how the door moved.

items.exampleCN: 他们以非暴力方式抗议。
fiercely 带有野兽般的火热。
轻轻地关上被猛烈打开的门。

definition_zh: 生动的；鲜明的；栩栩如生的；鲜艳的
definition_en: producing clear, strong pictures in the mind, as if seen rather than read
core_image: 一扇门推开，颜色和声音一齐涌到眼前
scene: 合上书以后，那个夏天的画面还在脑子里亮着，蝉声、树影和汗味都像刚发生。 Her description of the village was so vivid that we could smell the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 vivid 是「生动的」（第 1 个义项：让人脑中浮出清晰画面与感知）；句意为她对村庄的描述太生动，我们仿佛闻到了雨味。颜色和声音一齐涌来的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 生动的；鲜艳的；栩栩如生的

senses.title: Clear enough to seem real
senses.definition: so full of detail that the mind seems to see or hear the thing itself
senses.definitionCN: 细节丰富到脑中仿佛真的看见或听见
senses.example: Her description of the village was so vivid that we could smell the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她对村庄的描述如此生动，我们仿佛闻到了雨味。
senses.why: The root means alive, and a description that makes an absent thing seem present behaves as if it were alive.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「活着」，而让不在场之物如同在场的描写，也就表现得像活着一样。

senses.title: Strong and bright in colour
senses.definition: of colours, strong, clean and immediately noticeable
senses.definitionCN: 形容颜色时指强烈、纯净、一眼就能注意到
senses.example: The doors of the old town are painted in vivid blue and green.
senses.exampleCN: 老城的门被涂成鲜艳的蓝色和绿色。
senses.why: Colour is what makes a scene jump at the eye, so the same adjective passes from detail to hue.
senses.whyCN: 颜色正是让景象直扑眼睛的东西，于是同一个形容词从细节转到色调。

senses.title: Strongly held in memory or imagination
senses.definition: of a memory, dream or image, remaining clear and forceful over time
senses.definitionCN: 形容记忆、梦或形象，久久保持清晰而强烈
senses.example: He still had a vivid picture of the first snowfall at home.
senses.exampleCN: 他对家乡第一场雪仍有一幅清晰的画面。
senses.why: What is vivid in the moment is exactly what refuses to fade, so memory and imagination are described the same way.
senses.whyCN: 当下鲜明的，正是最不肯褪色的，于是记忆与想象用了同一个形容。

senses.title: Full of life in manner
senses.definition: in older use of a person, lively and full of animation
senses.definitionCN: 旧时形容人时指活泼有生气
senses.example: Her vivid manner made the dull meeting short.
senses.exampleCN: 她活泼的举止让这场沉闷的会变短了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply alive, and the word still carries that warmth when applied to people.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层就是「有生命」，用在人身上时这层暖意仍在。

intro.en: Vivid comes from Latin vividus, lively, from vivere, to live.
intro.cn: vivid 来自拉丁语 vividus（有生气的），源出 vivere（活）。

items.en: Vivere meant to live; vividus described what was full of life or long-lived.
items.cn: vivere 意为活着，vividus 形容充满生气或长存不灭的东西。

items.en: Roman writers applied vividus to colours, to speech and to light, not only to living bodies.
items.cn: 罗马作家把 vividus 用在颜色、言语与光上，不只用于活物。

items.en: The same root gave vivere’s siblings, including vivax, tenacious of life, and vivus, alive.
items.cn: 同一词根还生出 vivax（生命力顽强）与 vivus（活的）。

items.en: English adopted vivid in the seventeenth century for bright colour and lively writing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入 vivid，用于鲜亮的颜色与活泼的文字。

items.en: Modern use keeps the double force: bright to the eye, and clear to the mind's eye.
items.cn: 现代用法保留了两重力量：眼睛看到鲜亮，心眼看到清晰。

note.en: The first group gathers the life root, the second the adjectives of bright and clear description.
note.cn: 第一组收「生命」词根，第二组收形容鲜明与清晰描写之词。

entries.definition: The adverb, in a lively and clear manner.
The quality that makes a scene seem real.
Lively in manner, said of people.
To bring to life or make lively.
So detailed that it is almost unpleasant to read.
entries.definitionCN: 描写具体到令人不适的

entries.definition: Strong in colour or light.
Without clear shape or detail.
Long and dull, sharing the root but with the life gone.
entries.definitionCN: 冗长乏味的，同词根却没了生气

normalIntro.en: The root is to live; what is vivid is alive in the eye, in the memory and in the describing words.
normalIntro.cn: 词根是「活」，凡是 vivid 的东西，都在眼睛里、记忆里和描述的文字里活着。

normal.en: Viv- is life, so a vivid scene is one that lives in the mind.
normal.cn: viv- 是生命，vivid 的场景就是活在心里。

normal.en: Vivid colours are strong; vivid writing is detailed.
normal.cn: vivid colours 指颜色强烈，vivid writing 指文字细致。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ly and keeps the same spelling.
normal.cn: 副词加 -ly，拼写不变。

normal.en: Same root as survive, which means to live through.
normal.cn: 与 survive 同根，后者意为活过来。

normal.en: Its opposite is vague, with no edges.
normal.cn: 反义是 vague，没有边角。

abstract.en: See a deep blue door on a grey street.
abstract.cn: 想灰街上的一扇深蓝的门。

abstract.en: Hear a story told so well that rain seems to fall in the room.
abstract.cn: 听一个讲得太好的故事，屋里仿佛下起雨来。

abstract.en: Feel a memory stay sharp after years.
abstract.cn: 感受一段记忆多年后仍然锐利。

examples.en: The book gives a vivid account of life at sea.
examples.cn: 这本书生动地讲述了海上生活。

examples.en: She has vivid memories of her first day at school.
examples.cn: 她对上学的第一天有清晰的记忆。

examples.en: The garden was full of vivid red flowers.
examples.cn: 花园里满是鲜艳的红花。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威威的」——颜色威威地逼上前来，画面也威威地留在脑里。

root: 拉丁语 vivere（活）→ vividus（有生气的）→ 英语 vivid；同源词有 survive、revive、vivacity。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins at being alive and ends by lending that life to descriptions, colours, memories and even manners.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「活着」起步，最后把这份生气借给了描写、颜色、记忆甚至举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opening onto colour and sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门推开，颜色与声音涌来。

branches.en: The description branch: a village one can smell.
branches.cn: 描写分支：能闻到的村庄。

branches.en: The colour branch: bright blue and green doors.
branches.cn: 颜色分支：鲜蓝与鲜绿的门。

branches.en: The memory branch: the first snowfall at home.
branches.cn: 记忆分支：家乡的第一场雪。

branches.en: The manner branch: a dull meeting made short.
branches.cn: 举止分支：沉闷的会变短了。

branches.en: The storytelling branch: words that leave a picture behind.
branches.cn: 讲叙分支：留下画面的文字。

intro.en: The life root viv- takes -id for the adjective, -ly for the adverb and -acious for the manner word.
intro.cn: 生命词根 viv- 加 -id 成形容词，加 -ly 成副词，加 -acious 成形容举止的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vivere, vividus and vivax are all recorded, and the root also survives in survive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vivere、vividus、vivax 均有文献，这个词根也存活在 survive 之中。

items.example: It is the root of the family.
It is shortened to -vive in survive.
The English word came almost unchanged.
It forms survive, to live beyond.

definition_zh: 循环；流通；发行量
definition_en: the movement of blood around the body, the passing of money or news among people, or the number of copies of a publication sold
core_image: 报纸从印刷机上一叠叠装车送走
scene: 报摊上的报纸一早就被取空，印刷机还在转。 The magazine has a circulation of half a million.
sceneCN: 这里 circulation 指「发行量」（第 3 个义项：报刊每期售出的份数）；句意是这本杂志的发行量有五十万份。

senses.title: Movement of blood
senses.definition: the movement of blood around the body
senses.definitionCN: 血液在全身的流动
senses.example: Exercise improves the circulation.
senses.exampleCN: 运动能改善血液循环。
senses.why: Latin circulatio named the act of moving in a ring, and blood was the first thing described.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 circulatio 指沿环移动，血液是最早被描述的对象。

senses.title: Passing among people
senses.definition: the passing of money, goods or news among people
senses.definitionCN: 货币、货物或消息在人群中的流转
senses.example: New coins are now in circulation.
senses.exampleCN: 新硬币现在已在流通。
senses.why: Money and news follow the same loop as blood in a body.
senses.whyCN: 货币与消息遵循的正是血液在体内那样的环路。

senses.title: Copies sold or sent out
senses.definition: the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine sold
senses.definitionCN: 报刊每期售出的份数
senses.example: The magazine has a circulation of half a million.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志的发行量有五十万份。
senses.why: The number of copies sent round measures how far the paper travels.
senses.whyCN: 绕着送出的份数，衡量的就是这份报纸走得有多远。

intro.en: Circulation is the Latin noun of action for moving in a ring.
intro.cn: circulation 是表示沿环移动的拉丁语动作名词。

items.en: Circulus named a small ring.
items.cn: circulus 指小圆环。

items.en: Circulare meant to move something round.
items.cn: circulare 意为使某物绕行。

items.en: Circulatio named the act of going round.
items.cn: circulatio 指绕行的动作。

items.en: English circulation first described the blood.
items.cn: 英语 circulation 最初描述血液的流动。

items.en: The word extended to money, news and printed copies.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到货币、消息与印刷份数。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin ring root, while the meaning group names flows and reach.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语圆环词根，近义组列出流动与覆盖范围。

entries.definition: a round closed shape
shaped like a circle
a closed path for electric current
a steady movement of liquid or air
entries.definitionCN: 液体或空气平稳的流动

entries.definition: the act of giving out to many people
the people who read a publication
entries.definitionCN: 阅读某份出版物的人群

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ion noun ending, the blood image and the newspaper number.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 -ion 名词词尾、血液意象以及报刊份数。

normal.en: Circulation is the noun of circulate, so the ending -ion marks the act.
normal.cn: circulation 是 circulate 的名词，-ion 词尾标记动作。

normal.en: Blood circulation, money circulation, newspaper circulation: three loops of different size.
normal.cn: blood circulation、money circulation、newspaper circulation，三个大小不同的环。

normal.en: In circulation means out among people, not locked in a drawer.
normal.cn: in circulation 指在人群里流转，而不是锁在抽屉里。

normal.en: A magazine with a large circulation reaches many hands each month.
normal.cn: 发行量大的杂志每个月能到许多人手里。

normal.en: Withdraw from circulation is the opposite path, taking money or goods out of the loop.
normal.cn: withdraw from circulation 是相反的路径，把钱或货从环里取出。

abstract.en: Picture a warm pulse moving from the wrist up the arm.
abstract.cn: 想象温热的脉搏从手腕一路向上走。

abstract.en: Picture a coin passing through five hands in one day.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币一天里经过五个人的手。

abstract.en: Picture stacked papers sliding into a delivery van.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠叠报纸滑进送货车里。

examples.en: Cold hands are a sign of poor circulation.
examples.cn: 手发凉是循环不好的迹象。

examples.en: The old notes were taken out of circulation.
examples.cn: 旧纸币被停止流通。

examples.en: The paper doubled its circulation in one year.
examples.cn: 这家报纸一年内发行量翻了一倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: circulation 与 circulate 同根：绕一圈送出的份数，就是发行量。

root: 源自拉丁语 circulatio（绕行），由 circulare（使成环）派生，本指沿环流动，后指报刊绕送的份数。

sensesIntro.en: The act of moving in a ring starts with blood, then covers money and news, and finally counts the copies sent out.
sensesIntro.cn: 沿环移动先落在血液上，再覆盖货币与消息，最后用来数绕着送出的份数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: printed sheets leaving the press in tight stacks.
core.cn: 核心意象：印好的纸一叠叠离开印刷机。

branches.en: Blood is the first and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 血液是最早也最具体的义项。

branches.en: Money and news repeat the bodily loop in society.
branches.cn: 货币与消息在社会中重复身体里的环。

branches.en: The count of copies measures the width of the loop.
branches.cn: 份数衡量的是这个环有多宽。

branches.en: Body and economy share one noun of continuous flow.
branches.cn: 身体与经济共用一个表示持续流动的名词。

branches.en: A paper in circulation earns its circulation figure.
branches.cn: 在流通中的报纸才挣得它的发行量数字。

intro.en: The noun stem builds a plural, an adjective and the verb it comes from.
intro.cn: 这个名词词干构成复数、一个形容词以及它由之而来的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin circulatio grows from circulare, and -ion marks the resulting action noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circulatio 由 circulare 长出，-ion 标记由此形成的动作名词。

items.example: The two papers report different circulations.
items.exampleCN: 两家报纸公布的发行量不同。

items.example: Air must circulate behind the fridge.
The tank has a circular base.
items.exampleCN: 这个罐子有一个圆形底座。

items.example: The circle is drawn in chalk.

latinEntries.example: Circulatio is the direct source of circulation.
latinEntries.exampleCN: circulatio 是 circulation 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 进化；演变；发展
definition_en: a slow process of change and development
core_image: 一条从鱼到鸟再到人的细线图
scene: 化石记录展示了鸟类翅膀在漫长岁月中的演变。 The fossil record shows the evolution of bird wings over a very long time.
sceneCN: 这里 evolution 是「演变、进化」（第 1 个义项：缓慢变化发展的过程）；句意：化石记录展示了鸟类翅膀在漫长岁月中的演变。

senses.title: Biological change
senses.definition: the slow change of living things over generations
senses.definitionCN: 生物经过许多世代发生的缓慢变化
senses.example: Evolution explains how species adapt.
senses.exampleCN: 进化论解释了物种如何适应环境。
senses.why: The Latin root volvere means to roll, and unfolding is a kind of rolling out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 volvere 意为滚，展开就是滚开。

senses.title: Gradual development
senses.definition: a slow change in ideas or systems
senses.definitionCN: 思想或制度的缓慢变化
senses.example: The evolution of language never stops.
senses.exampleCN: 语言的演变从未停止。
senses.why: The word extends from species to anything that develops.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从物种延伸到任何发展中的事物。

senses.title: An unfolding movement
senses.definition: a planned movement of troops or ships
senses.definitionCN: 部队或舰船的有计划移动
senses.example: The general ordered a careful evolution of the fleet.
senses.exampleCN: 将军命令舰队谨慎变换队形。
senses.why: The oldest sense is an unfolding or unrolling.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是展开或铺开。

intro.en: Evolution comes from Latin evolutio, an unrolling, from evolvere.
intro.cn: evolution 源自拉丁语 evolutio（展开），来自 evolvere。

items.en: Volvere means to roll.
items.cn: volvere 意为滚。

items.en: Evolvere means to roll out or unroll.
items.cn: evolvere 意为滚出或展开。

items.en: Evolutio names an unrolling.
items.cn: evolutio 指展开。

items.en: Evolution first names an unfolding movement.
items.cn: evolution 最初指展开的动作。

items.en: It comes to mean the slow change of species.
items.cn: 它逐渐指物种的缓慢变化。

note.en: Evolution is gradual change; revolution is a sudden complete turn.
note.cn: evolution 是渐进变化；revolution 是突然的彻底翻转。

entries.definition: to change slowly into a new form
relating to evolution
a supporter of evolution theory
the process of growing or changing
the process of becoming larger
movement toward a better state

normalIntro.en: Evolution is a long scroll slowly unrolling through time.
normalIntro.cn: evolution 是随时间缓缓展开的长卷。

normal.en: The theory of evolution explains species change.
normal.cn: 进化论解释物种变化。

normal.en: Human evolution took millions of years.
normal.cn: 人类进化历经数百万年。

normal.en: The evolution of language is easy to see.
normal.cn: 语言的演变很容易看出来。

normal.en: Gradual evolution means slow change.
normal.cn: gradual evolution 意为缓慢变化。

normal.en: Compare revolution: evolution unfolds, revolution overturns.
normal.cn: 对比 revolution：evolution 展开，revolution 推翻。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line changing from fish to bird to human.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细线从鱼变到鸟再变到人。

abstract.en: Imagine a scroll unrolling one small picture at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象长卷一次展开一幅小图。

abstract.en: Think of a path that changes shape as it goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一条边走边改变形状的路。

examples.en: Evolution takes place over many generations.
examples.cn: 进化经过许多世代才发生。

examples.en: The book traces the evolution of the bicycle.
examples.cn: 这本书追溯了自行车的演变。

examples.en: Scientists study the evolution of bird wings.
examples.cn: 科学家研究鸟类翅膀的进化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ volution（转）」——慢慢转出来、展开来，就是进化与演变。

root: 拉丁语 evolvere（展开）＝ e-（出）＋ volvere（滚）→ evolutio → evolution，核心义「逐渐展开」。

sensesIntro.en: Evolution starts as an unrolling, becomes biological change, and also names gradual development in any field.
sensesIntro.cn: evolution 从展开开始，成为生物变化，也指任何领域的逐渐发展。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line changing from fish to bird to human.
core.cn: 核心意象：从鱼到鸟再到人的细线。

branches.en: Biological change is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 生物变化是现代主要含义。

branches.en: Any system can slowly evolve.
branches.cn: 任何体系都能缓慢演变。

branches.en: The old sense is an unfolding movement.
branches.cn: 古老含义是展开的动作。

branches.en: Species and languages both unfold over time.
branches.cn: 物种与语言都随时间展开。

branches.en: The unrolling image underlies both meanings.
branches.cn: 展开的意象支撑两种含义。

intro.en: Evolution combines e-, out, the root volv, to roll, and the suffix -ion.
intro.cn: evolution 由 e-（出）、词根 volv（滚）与后缀 -ion 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin evolvere and evolutio give the word its shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 evolvere 与 evolutio 赋予这个词形态。

definition_zh: 太阳的；太阳能的
definition_en: relating to the sun, or powered by the sun's energy
core_image: 屋顶上一排面向太阳的蓝色电池板
scene: 屋顶安装了太阳能板。 Solar panels were fitted on the roof.
sceneCN: 这里 solar 是「太阳能的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：屋顶安装了太阳能板。

senses.title: Of the sun
senses.definition: relating to the sun
senses.definitionCN: 与太阳相关的
senses.example: The solar system has eight planets.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳系有八颗行星。
senses.why: This is the astronomical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是天文学义项。

senses.title: Powered by the sun
senses.definition: using energy from the sun
senses.definitionCN: 使用来自太阳的能量的
senses.example: Solar panels were fitted on the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶安装了太阳能板。
senses.why: Modern use names technology that draws on sunlight.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法指利用阳光的技术。

intro.en: Solar comes from Latin solaris, belonging to the sun.
intro.cn: solar 来自拉丁语 solaris，意为属于太阳的。

items.en: Sol meant the sun.
items.cn: sol 意为太阳。

items.en: Solaris meant relating to the sun.
items.cn: solaris 意为与太阳相关的。

items.en: The word entered English as solar.
items.cn: 这个词以 solar 进入英语。

items.en: It described the sun and the system around it.
items.cn: 它描述太阳及其周围系统。

items.en: It came to name power taken from sunlight.
items.cn: 它开始指从阳光取得的能源。

note.en: Solar is compared with look-alike words and words for sky and energy.
note.cn: 把 solar 与形近词以及表示天空和能源的词作比较。

entries.definition: hard and firm
relating to the North or South Pole
a person who studies a subject deeply
relating to the moon
full of bright sunlight
relating to stars

normalIntro.en: Solar ties a thing to the sun, either its family or its power.
normalIntro.cn: solar 把事物与太阳联系起来，或是它的家族，或是它的能量。

normal.en: Solar panels were fitted on the roof.
normal.cn: 屋顶安装了太阳能板。

normal.en: The solar system has eight planets.
normal.cn: 太阳系有八颗行星。

normal.en: Solar energy is clean and renewable.
normal.cn: 太阳能清洁且可再生。

normal.en: A solar eclipse darkened the morning.
normal.cn: 日食让早晨变暗。

normal.en: The farm runs on solar power.
normal.cn: 这个农场靠太阳能电力运转。

abstract.en: Nearly everything alive is spending stored sunlight.
abstract.cn: 几乎一切生命都在花储存起来的阳光。

abstract.en: The sun asks for no payment and keeps no receipt.
abstract.cn: 太阳不索报酬，也不留收据。

abstract.en: We are a small family around a very large fire.
abstract.cn: 我们是一大团火旁的一个小家庭。

examples.en: Solar panels were fitted on the roof.
examples.cn: 屋顶安装了太阳能板。

examples.en: The solar system has eight planets.
examples.cn: 太阳系有八颗行星。

examples.en: Solar energy is clean and renewable.
examples.cn: 太阳能清洁且可再生。

dict_mnemonic.text: solar 与 solid 形近；solar energy 是「太阳能」，solar panel 是「太阳能板」。

root: 拉丁语 sol（太阳）加形容词词尾 -aris，核心义「属于太阳的」。

sensesIntro.en: Solar means relating to the sun or powered by the sun's energy.
sensesIntro.cn: solar 意为与太阳相关的，或由太阳能驱动的。

core.en: Everything that belongs to the sun.
core.cn: 属于太阳的一切。

branches.en: Planets circle one bright star.
branches.cn: 行星围绕一颗明亮的恒星运转。

branches.en: Panels turn sunlight into power.
branches.cn: 电池板把阳光变成电力。

branches.en: An eclipse hides the sun for minutes.
branches.cn: 日食让太阳隐没几分钟。

branches.en: The star and the power taken from it share one word.
branches.cn: 恒星与从它取得的能源共用一个词。

branches.en: A roof becomes a small power station.
branches.cn: 屋顶变成一座小小的电站。

intro.en: Solar builds words for sun power, systems, and sky events.
intro.cn: solar 构成表示太阳能、太阳系和天空现象的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root sol means the sun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词根 sol 意为太阳。

items.exampleCN: 太阳的热量温暖了房子。
太阳能电力供应这些灯。

items.meaning: the sun and the bodies around it

items.example: A solar eclipse drew crowds outside.
items.exampleCN: 日食把人群吸引到户外。

items.meaning: a stream of particles from the sun
items.example: The solar wind reaches the earth.

latinEntries.example: Sol is Latin for the sun.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sol 是拉丁语中的太阳。

definition_zh: 钱包；皮夹；钱夹
definition_en: a small flat case, often of leather, for carrying money, cards and papers
core_image: 一个对折的皮夹，翻开是几张卡和折起的钞票
scene: 结账时他从后袋里掏出那个被磨得发白的皮夹，抽出卡递过去。 He found his wallet was gone when he reached the ticket desk.
sceneCN: 这里 wallet 是「钱包」（第 1 个义项：装钱、卡与票证的小扁平夹子）；句意为他走到售票台时发现钱包不见了。磨白的对折皮夹那幅画就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A case for money and cards
senses.definition: a small flat folding case for carrying notes, cards and a few papers
senses.definitionCN: 装纸币、卡与少量证件的小型对折扁平夹子
senses.example: He found his wallet was gone when he reached the ticket desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他走到售票台时发现钱包不见了。
senses.why: The word came from a bag for the back and for travel, and the money case is only its latest job.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指背在背上或旅行用的袋子，装钱只是它最近的一份工作。

senses.title: Older words for a bag
senses.definition: in old British use, a bag or knapsack carried when travelling
senses.definitionCN: 旧英式用法中指旅行时携带的袋子或背包
senses.example: The boy set off with a wallet of clothes over his shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 那男孩肩上挎着一包衣服就出发了。
senses.why: The bag sense came first, and a few dialects keep it for a bundle of clothes or food.
senses.whyCN: 袋子这一层来得最早，少数方言里仍用它指一包衣服或食物。

senses.title: A small case of papers
senses.definition: in old use, a case for papers or tools rather than for money
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法中指而不是装钱的文件或工具夹
senses.example: The surveyor kept his maps in a canvas wallet.
senses.exampleCN: 测量员把地图放在一只帆布夹里。
senses.why: Before it meant money, the word named any flat case that carried papers, and this use survives in a few trades.
senses.whyCN: 在指钱之前，这个词泛指装纸件的扁平夹，这一用法在少数行业里仍存。

senses.title: A digital holding place
senses.definition: now also a phone service or app that stores money and cards
senses.definitionCN: 如今也指在手机里存放钱与卡的软件服务
senses.example: Many people now pay from a wallet on their phone.
senses.exampleCN: 如今很多人用手机里的电子钱包付款。
senses.why: A wallet is a holding place, so the app that holds money simply takes the old name.
senses.whyCN: 钱包就是个盛放之处，于是装钱的软件直接沿用了这个旧名。

intro.en: Wallet is from Old French walet, a bag or a roll carried for travel, of uncertain older origin.
intro.cn: wallet 来自古法语 walet，指旅行用的袋子或铺盖卷，更早的来源不甚确定。

items.en: Walet meant a bag, a knapsack, or a roll of bedding carried on the back.
items.cn: walet 意为袋子、背包，或背在背上的铺盖卷。

items.en: The word probably goes back to a Germanic root for rolling or turning over, which fits a bedroll.
items.cn: 这个词大概追溯到日耳曼语表示滚动、翻卷的词根，正好合于铺盖卷。

items.en: English took it for a bag of food and clothes for a journey, and later for a small case.
items.cn: 英语先用它指旅途中的食物与衣物袋，后来才指小夹子。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the leather case for notes and cards had taken over the meaning.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，装纸币与卡片的皮夹终于占了这一词义。

items.en: The digital wallet of the twenty-first century repeats the pattern: an old word for a holding place.
items.cn: 二十一世纪的电子钱包重复了同一模式：一个古老表示「盛放之处」的词。

note.en: The first group gathers the money-case family, the second the other receptacles for money and papers.
note.cn: 第一组收装钱的夹子类词，第二组收其他装钱与票据的器物。

entries.definition: The plural form, with -s.
A wallet kept in a phone.
A small bag for money, now often a woman’s.
The American word for a folding wallet.
Any container with a lid or a fold.
A small holder for cards only.
A soft container with an opening, larger than a wallet.
Where money is held without any case at all.

normalIntro.en: Wallet began as a travelling bag, so the memory can start from a bag over the shoulder and shrink to a pocket.
normalIntro.cn: wallet 起初是旅行袋，可以从肩上那只袋子想起，再缩到口袋里。

normal.en: A wallet was once a bag; now it fits in a pocket.
normal.cn: wallet 曾是袋子，如今装进衣袋。

normal.en: British purse and American billfold overlap with it.
normal.cn: 英式 purse 与美式 billfold 都与它重叠。

normal.en: An e-wallet is a wallet without leather.
normal.cn: e-wallet 是没有皮革的钱包。

normal.en: You open a wallet and lose a wallet; both are common.
normal.cn: open a wallet 与 lose a wallet 都很常用。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with walet, the French bag it came from.
normal.cn: 别与它的法语来源 walet（袋子）混淆。

abstract.en: See a worn fold showing at the back pocket.
abstract.cn: 想后袋露出的那道磨白的折边。

abstract.en: Hear cards click as the case opens.
abstract.cn: 听夹子打开时卡片一响。

abstract.en: Picture a phone paying for a bus fare.
abstract.cn: 想一部手机刷开车费。

examples.en: He pulled a few notes from his wallet.
examples.cn: 他从钱包里抽出几张钞票。

examples.en: She keeps her tickets in the front of her wallet.
examples.cn: 她把车票放在钱包的前层。

examples.en: Losing your wallet abroad is always difficult.
examples.cn: 在国外丢钱包总是很麻烦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「窝了它」——钱有个窝，一折起来就把它们窝了它在里头。

root: 古法语 walet（旅行袋；铺盖卷），更早或出自日耳曼语表示滚动、翻卷的词根，来源不甚确定。

sensesIntro.en: A travelling bag shrinks into a pocket case, and the same name now covers the phone that holds your money.
sensesIntro.cn: 一只旅行袋缩成口袋里的夹子，同一个名字如今又罩住了装钱的手机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn leather fold.
core.cn: 核心意象：磨白的皮折。

branches.en: The pocket branch: missing at the ticket desk.
branches.cn: 口袋分支：售票台前不见了。

branches.en: The travel branch: a bag of clothes on one shoulder.
branches.cn: 旅行分支：肩上挎一包衣服。

branches.en: The papers branch: maps in a canvas case.
branches.cn: 证件分支：帆布夹里的地图。

branches.en: The digital branch: paying by phone.
branches.cn: 数字分支：用手机付款。

branches.en: The money branch: notes in leather or in an app.
branches.cn: 钱财分支：钞票在皮革里或在应用里。

intro.en: Wallet is a whole borrowed word; the modern family is made of compounds such as e-wallet.
intro.cn: wallet 是整词借入，现代词族由 e-wallet 这类复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the word came from Old French and possibly a Germanic root, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，出自古法语，可能上溯日耳曼词根，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: The direct source of the word.
It forms billfold, the American counterpart.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 billfold，美式对应词。

definition_zh: 错误的；不正确的；基于误判的
definition_en: wrong or based on a mistake
core_image: 一个人偏离了直路，走进岔道还以为是正途
scene: 报告里有一个错误的数据，结论因此站不住脚。 The report contained an erroneous figure, so its conclusion failed.
sceneCN: 这里 erroneous 是「错误的」（第 1 个义项：事实或内容不正确）；句意：报告里有一个错误的数据，所以结论站不住脚。

pos.zh: 错误的；不正确的；基于误判的

senses.title: Factually wrong
senses.definition: containing a mistake or not matching the facts
senses.definitionCN: 包含错误或与事实不符的
senses.example: The article was based on erroneous data.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章建立在错误的数据之上。
senses.why: The adjective comes from error, whose Latin root means wandering, so a wrong statement has strayed from the truth.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词来自 error，其拉丁词根意为「游荡」，所以错误的陈述偏离了真相。

senses.title: Based on mistaken judgment
senses.definition: formed from a wrong belief, assumption, or way of reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 建立在错误信念、假设或推理方式上的
senses.example: Their conclusion proved erroneous after further study.
senses.exampleCN: 进一步研究后，他们的结论被证明是错的。
senses.why: A mistaken judgment is a path of thought that has wandered off course.
senses.whyCN: 错误的判断就是一条偏离正轨的思路。

intro.en: Erroneous comes from Latin erroneus, wandering, from errare, to wander or stray.
intro.cn: erroneous 来自拉丁语 erroneus（游荡的），源于 errare（漫游、走偏）。

items.en: Errare means to wander or stray.
items.cn: errare 意为游荡、走偏。

items.en: Error means a wandering or a mistake.
items.cn: error 意为游荡或错误。

items.en: Erroneus means wandering or mistaken.
items.cn: erroneus 意为游荡的、错误的。

items.en: Erroneous enters English with the mistake sense.
items.cn: erroneous 以「错误」的含义进入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses erroneous mainly for beliefs and information.
items.cn: 现代英语中，erroneous 主要用于信念和信息。

note.en: Erroneous is the adjective of error, close to its family and to words for being wrong.
note.cn: erroneous 是 error 的形容词，与自身词族以及表示「错误」的词相邻。

entries.definition: a mistake
by mistake
wandering or straying
not right or true
wrong in opinion or judgment
not true

normalIntro.en: Erroneous comes from wandering: a wrong idea has walked off the true path.
normalIntro.cn: erroneous 来自「游荡」：错误的想法走离了正确的道路。

normal.en: Erroneous data leads to bad decisions.
normal.cn: 错误的数据导致糟糕的决定。

normal.en: An erroneous belief is a belief that is not true.
normal.cn: erroneous belief 是不符合事实的信念。

normal.en: The adverb erroneously means by mistake.
normal.cn: 副词 erroneously 表示错误地。

normal.en: The noun error is the simpler relative.
normal.cn: 名词 error 是更简单的亲属词。

normal.en: Compare mistaken: mistaken stresses the person, erroneous stresses the content.
normal.cn: 对比 mistaken：mistaken 强调人，erroneous 强调内容。

abstract.en: Picture a traveler taking the wrong fork in a road.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人在岔路口走错了方向。

abstract.en: Imagine a map with one line drawn in the wrong place.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上有一条线画错了位置。

abstract.en: Think of a calculator showing a number that cannot be right.
abstract.cn: 想象计算器显示出一个不可能正确的数字。

examples.en: The rumor turned out to be erroneous.
examples.cn: 那个谣言最终被证明是错的。

examples.en: An erroneous assumption ruined the whole plan.
examples.cn: 一个错误的假设毁掉了整个计划。

examples.en: Please correct any erroneous entries in the list.
examples.cn: 请更正清单中任何错误的条目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「error + neous」——带着「错误」的形容词，就是错误的；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 errare（游荡、走偏）→ error（错误）→ erroneus（游荡的、错误的）→ 英语 erroneous，核心义「偏离正途而错」。

sensesIntro.en: Erroneous first describes wrong facts or statements, and then wrong beliefs or ways of reasoning.
sensesIntro.cn: erroneous 先描述错误的事实或陈述，再描述错误的信念或推理方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path that has strayed away from the true road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条偏离正路的岔道。

branches.en: Wrong content is the main factual sense.
branches.cn: 内容错误是主要事实义项。

branches.en: Wrong judgment applies straying to reasoning.
branches.cn: 误判把「走偏」用于推理。

branches.en: Bad data and bad assumptions both lead reasoning astray.
branches.cn: 坏数据与坏假设都会把推理带偏。

branches.en: A statement and a figure can both be erroneous.
branches.cn: 陈述与数字都可能是错误的。

branches.en: A belief and a conclusion can both rest on error.
branches.cn: 信念与结论都可能建立在错误之上。

intro.en: Erroneous is a Latin wandering adjective, with English relatives error, erroneously, and erroneousness.
intro.cn: erroneous 是拉丁语中表示「走偏」的形容词，英语亲属有 error、erroneously 与 erroneousness。

latinIntro.en: Latin errare means to wander, and error means a wandering or mistake.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 errare 意为游荡，error 意为游荡或错误。

definition_zh: 发生；出现；事件；发生率；（矿物的）产出；出现次数
definition_en: the fact of something happening or existing, or an event that happens
core_image: 日历上某一天被红笔圈了一下，旁边只写了两个字：发生了。
scene: 保险报告统计过去五年同类事故的情况，发现多数集中在雨季。 The report counted the occurrence of similar accidents over five years.
sceneCN: 这里 occurrence 是“同类事件发生的次数、发生情况”（第 3 个义项）；句意：报告统计了过去五年同类事故的发生次数；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 发生；出现；事件；发生率；（矿物的）产出；出现次数

derivatives.zh: 正在发生的；偶然发生的

senses.title: Something that happens
senses.definition: an event or incident that takes place, especially one that is noticed
senses.definitionCN: 发生的事件或事故，尤指被注意到的一次
senses.example: The police logged every unusual occurrence at the border that night.
senses.exampleCN: 警方记录了那晚边境上每一件不寻常的事。
senses.why: The word can point at the thing itself: once an event has happened, it can be counted, listed, and reported like an object.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指向事情本身：事件一旦发生，就能像物件一样被计数、列举与报告。

senses.title: The fact of happening
senses.definition: the fact or process of something happening or existing
senses.definitionCN: 某事物发生或存在的事实与过程
senses.example: The occurrence of frost in June surprised the growers.
senses.exampleCN: 六月出现霜冻让种植户感到意外。
senses.why: Here the word names not the event but its coming into being; the emphasis is on 'that it happened at all'.
senses.whyCN: 这里命名的不是事件，而是它“产生”这一过程；重点在于“它竟然发生了”。

senses.title: How often it happens
senses.titleCN: 出现次数：一段时间里发生了几回
senses.definition: the number of times something happens within a stated period or group
senses.definitionCN: 某事物在特定时段或群体内发生的次数
senses.example: The occurrence of the error fell by half after the new check was added.
senses.exampleCN: 加入新检查后，该错误的发生次数减少了一半。
senses.why: Counting turns an event into a rate; agencies need the count, not the story of any single case.
senses.whyCN: 计数把事件变成比率；机构需要的是次数，而不是任何单个案例的故事。

senses.title: A rate in statistics
senses.titleCN: 发生率：分母里的那批人
senses.definition: the proportion of a population in which a specified event happens over a period
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内，特定事件在某一群体中发生的比例
senses.example: The occurrence rate of the side effect was two cases per thousand patients.
senses.exampleCN: 该副作用的发生率为每千名患者两例。
senses.why: Statistics adds a denominator: the same number of cases means different things in a small town and a large city.
senses.whyCN: 统计学加上了分母：同样的病例数，在小镇和大城市意味着不同的事情。

senses.title: Something found in nature
senses.titleCN: 自然出现：不必人为制造
senses.definition: the presence of a substance, species, or phenomenon in the natural environment
senses.definitionCN: 某物质、物种或现象在自然环境中存在
senses.example: The natural occurrence of the mineral in local rock made mining cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 这种矿物在当地岩石中天然产出，使开采成本很低。
senses.why: The word reports existence without agency: no one made it happen, it is simply found where conditions allowed it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词报告的是“存在”而非“作为”：无人使它发生，它只是在条件允许的地方被找到。

senses.title: A mineral showing in rock
senses.titleCN: 矿点：地质图上标出的那一处
senses.definition: a deposit or showing of a mineral in a particular place, as recorded in geology
senses.definitionCN: 地质记录中某地矿物的矿床或露头
senses.example: The survey marked three occurrences of copper in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 勘测在山谷里标出了三处铜矿点。
senses.why: Geology gives the word a spatial sense: an occurrence is where the mineral 'turns up', a point on a map rather than a moment in time.
senses.whyCN: 地质学给这个词一个空间义：occurrence 是矿物“露面”的地点，是地图上的一点，而不是时间中的一刻。

senses.title: A word appearing in text
senses.titleCN: 出现：某个词在文本里露了几次
senses.definition: an instance of a linguistic item appearing in a text or corpus
senses.definitionCN: 某一语言项在文本或语料库中出现的一次实例
senses.example: The corpus records each occurrence of the phrase with its source line.
senses.exampleCN: 语料库记录该短语的每一次出现及其所在行。
senses.why: Linguistics counts tokens: every time the same form appears, it is a separate occurrence, even though the word is one.
senses.whyCN: 语言学数的是“个例”：同一形式每出现一次就是一个独立的 occurrence，尽管那个词只有一个。

senses.title: A case of disease
senses.titleCN: 病例出现：医院登记的那一例
senses.definition: a single diagnosed case of a disease in a population under surveillance
senses.definitionCN: 监测群体中被诊断出的一例疾病
senses.example: The health office reported the first occurrence of the new strain in March.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生部门报告了这种新毒株在三月首次出现。
senses.why: Public health treats each case as a countable unit; the word then means 'one more instance has entered the record'.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生把每一例当作可计数的单位；这个词于是表示“记录里又多了一例”。

intro.en: Occurrence comes from Latin occurrentia, from occurrere, to run to meet: ob- 'toward, against' plus currere 'to run'. The same verb gives occur and current.
intro.cn: occurrence 来自拉丁语 occurrentia，出自 occurrere“跑过去相遇”：ob-“朝向、对着”加 currere“跑”。同一动词给出 occur 与 current。

items.en: Currere meant to run. It underlies current, course, cursor, and excursion, all involving movement along a path.
items.cn: currere 意为跑。它构成 current、course、cursor、excursion，这些都涉及沿路径的运动。

items.en: Ob- plus currere meant to run up against something, hence to meet it, to present itself, or to come to mind.
items.cn: ob- 加 currere 意为跑上去撞见某物，因而表示相遇、浮现，或想起。

items.en: The noun named the act of meeting or turning up, and later a thing that turns up.
items.cn: 该名词指相遇或出现的行为，后来指出现的事物。

items.en: French occurrence kept the sense of an event that presents itself, especially something unexpected.
items.cn: 法语 occurrence 保留“自行出现的事件”之义，尤指意外之事。

items.en: English occurrence first meant a happening or an incident, then extended to frequency and to the presence of substances in nature.
items.cn: 英语 occurrence 最初指发生的事情或事件，随后扩展到频次，以及物质在自然中的存在。

items.en: Statistics, geology, linguistics, and medicine each gave the word a technical count: rate, deposit, token, case.
items.cn: 统计学、地质学、语言学与医学各自给这个词一个技术性计数：比率、矿点、个例、病例。

note.en: The first group is the occur family; the second compares words for things that happen, from the neutral event to the unexpected incident.
note.cn: 第一组是 occur 词族；第二组比较表示“发生之事”的词，从中性的事件到意外的变故。

entries.definition: to happen or exist; also to come into the mind. It names the event's coming about.
entries.definitionCN: 发生、存在；也指被想到；命名的是事件的发生。

entries.definition: to happen again, especially at intervals. The prefix re- adds repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 再次发生，尤指有间隔地复发；前缀 re- 增加重复义。

entries.definition: happening at a particular time; also used in philosophy for what is present.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一时刻发生的；哲学中也指当下呈现的。

entries.definition: anything that happens, especially something planned or notable. It is the broadest word.
entries.definitionCN: 发生的任何事，尤指计划中的或值得注意的；是最宽泛的词。

entries.definition: an event, often minor or unpleasant, that interrupts normal activity.
entries.definitionCN: 打断正常活动的意外事件，常较轻微或不愉快。

entries.definition: a single example or case of something general. It stresses the sample, not the happening.
entries.definitionCN: 一般事物的单个例子或案例；侧重样本，而非发生。

entries.definition: the number of times something happens in a period. It measures the count, not the event.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物在一段时间内发生的次数；测量计数，而非事件。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ob- 'against' plus currere 'to run', then -ence. Something that runs up against you has occurred.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ob-“对着”加 currere“跑”，再加 -ence。跑上来撞见你的东西，就是“发生了”。

normal.en: Occurrence is a run-in: something came along the path and met the moment.
normal.cn: occurrence 是一次撞见：某物沿路跑来，撞上了那个时刻。

normal.en: A red circle on the calendar marks one occurrence; the tally beside it counts them all.
normal.cn: 日历上的红圈标出一次 occurrence；旁边的计数把它们全数出来。

normal.en: Geology puts occurrence on a map; statistics puts it in a rate.
normal.cn: 地质学把 occurrence 放到地图上；统计学把它放进比率里。

normal.en: Every occurrence of a word in a corpus is one more token, even if the word is one.
normal.cn: 语料库里每出现一次该词就是一个新的个例，尽管那个词只有一个。

normal.en: A rare occurrence is news; a common occurrence is weather.
normal.cn: 罕见的事是新闻；常见的事是天气。

abstract.en: Occurrence is the most neutral word for change: it reports that something met the world, without saying why.
abstract.cn: occurrence 是关于变化最中性的词：它报告某物遇上了世界，却不解释原因。

abstract.en: Counting occurrences turns a story into a rate, and a rate is easier to compare than a story.
abstract.cn: 统计发生次数把故事变成比率，而比率比故事更容易比较。

abstract.en: What counts as an occurrence depends on where the observer draws the boundary of the event.
abstract.cn: 什么算作一次 occurrence，取决于观察者把事件的边界画在哪里。

examples.en: Flooding used to be a rare occurrence here, but the records now show it every other spring.
examples.cn: 这里过去很少发生洪水，但记录显示如今几乎隔年春天就有一次。

examples.en: The mineral's occurrence in the cliff was noted long before anyone tried to mine it.
examples.cn: 早在有人尝试开采之前，这种矿物在崖壁上的产出就已被记录。

examples.en: Each occurrence of the symbol in the manuscript was catalogued by hand.
examples.cn: 手稿中该符号的每一次出现都被手工编入目录。

dict_mnemonic.text: occur（发生）+ rence（名词）——发生的事、出现的次数，就是 occurrence。

root: 源自拉丁语 occurrentia，出自 occurrere“跑上去相遇”：ob-“对着”加 currere“跑”；本义为“迎面出现”，引申为“发生、事件、出现次数”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of occurrence. One idea holds them together: something turns up. It may turn up as a single event, as the fact of happening, as a count, as a rate, as a mineral in rock, as a word in a text, or as a case in a clinic.
sensesIntro.cn: occurrence 的八个义项由同一个观念维系：某物露面了。它可以是单个事件、发生这一事实、一个计数、一个比率、岩石中的矿物、文本中的词，或诊所里的一例病例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one day circled in red on a calendar, with two words beside it: it happened.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上某一天被红笔圈住，旁边写着两个字：发生了。

chain: LATIN OCCURRERE TO RUN UPON MEET
FRENCH OCCURRENCE AN EVENT THAT PRESENTS ITSELF
ENGLISH OCCURRENCE ANYTHING THAT TURNS UP

branches.en: THE THING AND THE FACT: an event that happened, and the bare fact that it happened.
branches.cn: 事情与事实：发生的事件，以及“它发生了”这一赤裸事实。

branches.en: COUNT AND RATE: how many times it turned up, and what proportion of a population it touched.
branches.cn: 次数与比率：它出现了多少回，以及它触及了群体中多大的比例。

branches.en: TURNING UP IN NATURE: a substance or species present without being made.
branches.cn: 在自然中露面：未被制造却已存在的物质或物种。

branches.en: TURNING UP IN SPACE AND TEXT: a mineral point on a map, a token in a corpus.
branches.cn: 在空间与文本中露面：地图上的矿点，语料库中的一个词例。

branches.en: TURNING UP IN THE CLINIC: one more diagnosed case entering the record.
branches.cn: 在诊所里露面：又一例确诊病例进入记录。

intro.en: Occurrence is occur plus -ence, the noun suffix for a state or an act. The family uses re- for happening again and -ent for the adjective.
intro.cn: occurrence 是 occur 加 -ence（表示状态或行为的名词后缀）。词族用 re- 表示再次发生，-ent 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is currere, to run, with ob- adding the meeting. Latin occurrere also meant to come to mind, which survives in the phrase 'it occurred to me'.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 currere“跑”，ob- 增加“相遇”之义。拉丁语 occurrere 也指“想起”，这一含义留在英语 it occurred to me 中。

items.meaning: to happen, or to come to mind
items.example: The accident occurred at the junction.

items.meaning: an event or the fact of happening
items.example: Power cuts are a daily occurrence in the old quarter.
The fever recurred after the treatment stopped.

items.meaning: a return of something after an interval
items.meaningCN: 某事物间隔一段时间后再次出现
items.example: The recurrence rate was lower in the second group.
The occurrent event was recorded but not explained.
items.exampleCN: 发生的事件被记录下来，却未得到解释。

items.example: Two concurrent storms hit the coast.
items.exampleCN: 两场风暴同时袭击了海岸。

items.meaning: a flow of water, air, or electricity; also present in time
items.meaningCN: 水流、气流或电流；也指当下的
items.example: The current carries the boat downstream.

items.meaning: the moving marker on a screen
items.example: The cursor stopped at the start of the line.

items.meaning: a short trip out and back
items.example: The class made a day excursion to the quarry.
items.exampleCN: 班级去采石场做了一日远足。

latinEntries.meaning: to run to meet, to present itself
